title: Milwaukee by Night
description: Milwaukee, late autumn 1991, after Psychomachia and a failed Sabbat infiltration. Four realms (Waking with Underground levels, Dreaming, Shadowlands, Near Umbra), Kindred domains, ~330 places and ~150 characters.

approx.name: Source gives the area; exact spot placed

waking.name: Waking
waking.banner: No Prince · the Sabbat beaten back · Velez still at large
waking.credit: Base map drawn from Milwaukee’s 1991 street grid and shoreline · positions approximate

levels.name: Underground
levels.banner: The Warrens · creatures in the tunnels · the Pocket under the lake
levels.credit: The sewers, the brewery caves and the Deep Tunnel (built 1986–1993) are real; everything living in them is improvised

dream.name: Dreaming
dream.banner: Nine Kithain · three freeholds · no court
dream.credit: The Dreaming keeps relationships before distances · dotted threads tie places to their mortal anchors

shadow.name: Shadowlands
shadow.banner: One Citadel · newly dead in the streets
shadow.credit: The Shadowlands remember what the living city has torn down · all wraith lore improvised

umbra.name: Umbra
umbra.banner: Three clans, one of them nearly gone · a poisoned forest
umbra.credit: The Penumbra mirrors the city’s spirit, not its streets · every zone, spirit and Garou here is improvised on the book’s Lupine lore

mecca.name: MECCA
mecca.sub: Milwaukee Exposition & Convention Center and Arena
mecca.html: The Versailles of Kindred Milwaukee: red carpet, crystal chandeliers, flowerbeds out front and extra police to keep the poor away. The Council meets here and several Elders keep havens in the complex. Anarch raids never get far past the lobby, where the ghoul Raoul and his armed team stand guard.

hyatt.name: Hyatt Regency
hyatt.html: Joined to MECCA by the sky-walk. Lucina keeps a permanent room on the 16th floor, and Carna’s favourite haven is here as well. In Council terms the Toreador and Tremere seats sleep under one roof.
hyatt.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 22; Lucina p. 48; Carna p. 53

arena.name: Milwaukee Arena
arena.html: Part of the sky-walked MECCA complex between the Auditorium and the Hyatt.

auditorium.name: Milwaukee Auditorium
auditorium.html: The Symphony plays here, a pleasure reserved for the most powerful Elders and Council members. Concerts are favourite negotiating venues: before a big vote, Councilmen whisper and pass notes between their private boxes, the music covering every word. Anarchs resent being shut out, and the Elders misread that anger as hatred of art.

reuss.name: H. Reuss Federal Plaza
reuss.html: The southern end of the sky-walk. Federal offices by day, a sheltered corridor for Elders by night.

journal.name: Milwaukee Journal building
journal.html: Directly across from MECCA. The greatest newspaper story of all time sleeps across the street, and the editors never notice. Merik even had a deal to read tomorrow’s edition early. The Elders find the arrangement very convenient.

police.name: Police Administration Building
police.html: Two blocks from MECCA. Since Merik died the department is a prize: Lucina wants the administration for anti-gang policy, Jason means to stop her, and Gracis is after the detectives who used to belong to Parovich. With Parovich exposed and destroyed, his informants in the detective bureau are masterless. Lieutenant James Wilks works out of here and knows more than he should.
police.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 24; The Pawns pp. 70–71

library.name: Milwaukee Public Library
library.html: An Elder haunt. Messages are hidden inside books, and the recipient is told which title to check out through a casual remark (“I’ve been reading about ancient Norwegian tools”). Deep in the second basement, off the card catalogue, sit magical tomes more than 600 years old. A Tremere would pay dearly for them.

firehq.name: Fire Department headquarters
firehq.html: Across from the Library. Gracis once controlled the department; when his men torched Hrothulf’s haven, the trucks took two hours to arrive. Hrothulf took the brigade for himself. If cornered, he could have the hoses fail and let the whole city burn.
firehq.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 23; The Fire Department p. 70

museum.name: Milwaukee Public Museum
museum.html: Once a Kindred favourite, until it displayed American Indian bones in an archaeological exhibit. Akawa has organised several attacks on the museum, and Lucina’s Toreador have retaliated without understanding his fury.

cityhall.name: City Hall
cityhall.html: Merik controlled the mayor’s office. Nobody has dared claim it since, because whoever holds the mayor can fire the police and fire chiefs and instantly make enemies of everyone who owns them. Gracis is weighing it. A losing Elder might grab it as a last resort and turn the game upside down.
cityhall.src: Milwaukee by Night, Downtown map #1; The Mayor p. 71

pabst.name: Pabst Theater
pabst.html: Shown on the book’s downtown map beside City Hall. A good stage for the city’s gilded diplomacy.

pac.name: Performing Arts Center
pac.html: Draws every kind of Kindred. The Council holds diplomacy sessions during performances. Late at night, Anarchs break in to stage mocking shows of their own.

merikpent.name: Merik’s penthouse (sealed)
merikpent.html: Plush rugs, spiced blood in crystal goblets, a herd of green-eyed vessels in the back rooms. By the end it held dried blood, dead flowers stapled to the walls and a drained aquarium. The book never gives an address; it is placed here atop an East Town tower inside the Elder core.
merikpent.src: Milwaukee by Night, Fire and Blood pp. 83–84; The Unmasking p. 114

stmary.name: Old St. Mary’s Church
stmary.html: An ordinary-looking church with a secret Inquisition base in its basement, where they share what they’ve learned about Vampires and Werewolves. The Kindred know. Merik’s standing order was to leave it alone in the hope the Inquisition would find nothing and go away. His death has changed that.

mac.name: Milwaukee Athletic Club
mac.html: In the middle of Union turf and a favourite hunting ground anyway. The members are young, fit and strong-hearted, so they can lose more blood safely and it flows faster.

artmuseum.name: Milwaukee Art Museum & War Memorial
artmuseum.html: Frequented by Toreador Elders who want to talk away from the Blood Brothers’ eyes, and the site of several secret Elder meetings about that gang. Turk’s Union keeps breaking in to deface the collection. The staff now pulls the best works at night and posts guards, but guards can be Dominated.

unionboat.name: The Union’s riverboat
unionboat.html: A broken-down paddle steamer moored on the Veterans Park shore, its bright banners hanging limp and grey. Turk sleeps here because he believes water makes it safe from fire, which he fears abnormally. The park’s homeless are the Union’s herd, so its members rarely fight short of blood.

crucible-mp.name: Missing Persons
crucible-mp.html: A crowd of several hundred every night and music that never gets wild. Kindred blend in easily and feed unnoticed, treating the patrons as a bloated, senseless herd.

crucible-dp.name: Deadman’s Party
crucible-dp.html: Neo-punk, avant-garde noise and the most outlandish drinks in town. A favourite of the Blood Brothers, and the police have been called more than once.

crucible-an.name: Arabian Nights
crucible-an.html: Desert murals and slow dances; a place to find a date if you have money. Elders who find modern music offensive settle for its soft, boring, blessedly quiet soundtrack.

crucible-pc.name: Peaches and Cream
crucible-pc.html: Constant sexual tension among the young, bored rich. Casanovas and Teases hunt here easily.

crucible-sb.name: Soldier Boy
crucible-sb.html: Camouflage netting, bayonets, dud grenades and Civil War cannonballs on the walls. The dance floor is tiny and the regulars know each other. Some old soldiers among the Kindred come only for the atmosphere.

crucible-hs.name: Howler & Starscape
crucible-hs.html: Two upscale clubs with $10–20 covers, floors of black steel and mirrors under coloured light. Loud, raucous, top-40. Nobody comes for the music.

marqint.name: Marquette Interchange
marqint.html: Where I-94 meets I-794 and I-43, small concrete courtyards are trapped between the ramps. Union gangers hop onto I-794, slip past Blood Brother lines and climb down into one; the Brothers arrive and battle is joined. No police patrol it, the homeless can’t get in, and more Anarch battles happen here than anywhere else.

mafia.name: The Don’s table, Third Ward
mafia.html: Gracis primarily controls the current Don and uses Mafia money for bribes and for mortal assassins who scare rivals. Capone of Chicago has quietly bought sway with some captains. Whoever thinks to use the drug pipeline could leash every street gang. Placed in the old Italian Third Ward.

h-gracis.name: Gracis’s villa
h-gracis.html: A fine 19th-century house that was his haven when he ran Kilbourntown, quaint and respectable outside, gaudy modern plastic within. The book says “along the waterfront north of Downtown”; placed on the Brewers Hill riverbank, the old north end of Kilbourntown.
h-gracis.src: Milwaukee by Night, Gracis p. 56; Scene 14 p. 107

h-scott.name: Sir Edward Scott’s flat
h-scott.html: His favourite of several homes: a small but elegant apartment on the east side near the lake, in the thick of Union turf, where the Black Prince was always welcome. Since his death in the invasion it stands empty; Union Anarchs still leave empty bottles and flowers by the door.

h-jason.name: Jason’s tenement penthouse
h-jason.html: A grand penthouse hidden inside a run-down little tenement; guests are shocked when the door opens. The book gives no neighbourhood; placed in Walker’s Point.

h-esau.name: Esau’s condo
h-esau.html: An expensive condo kept by the Malkavian in his Esau guise, hairier and more threatening. From here Esau coaches Turk against the Blood Brothers. Placed on Yankee Hill.

h-jacob.name: Jacob’s mansion
h-jacob.sub: Greendale, the edge of Kindred land
h-jacob.html: The Jacob personality keeps a mansion “on the very ends of Kindred-controlled territory in Greendale.” Two homes, one mind, and a war that has no end.

h-parovich.name: Parovich’s mansion (sealed)
h-parovich.html: A 19th-century ruin in one of the poorer parts of the Barrens, scheduled for demolition for years; Parovich kept pulling strings to save it. Sabbat messengers came and went. After his exposure the Council searched it and boarded it up: letters to Velez, a map of the tunnels, an empty coffin. Raul still haunts the steps. Placed among Concordia’s decaying Highland Boulevard mansions.
h-parovich.src: Milwaukee by Night, Parovich p. 44; Raul p. 46

h-anastasia.name: Anastasia’s steam tunnel
h-anastasia.html: A dry utility room under the high school she attended, as far from the hissing electrical gear as she can get, shared with a little zoo of stray cats. She moves between empty cellars and sewer drains. Placed under Washington High School.

h-kristian.name: Kristian’s borrowed basement
h-kristian.html: The basement of a house owned by an elderly couple who can barely get around upstairs. From here he hid Parovich’s fleeing childer and plotted his sire’s fall. Someone else got there first. Placed in Lincoln Village.

h-barth.name: Barth’s apartment
h-barth.html: A middle-class apartment in East downtown. Every weeknight from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. “Derik Dark” broadcasts on WBIT, slipping party and rumble notices to listening Kindred. He fears the Union will try to diablerize him.

h-louis.name: Louis Detonas’s apartment
h-louis.sub: Rugs like grass, a chandelier like stars
h-louis.html: A beautiful, spacious downtown apartment of extravagant luxury. Louis lied for Gracis about Hrothulf during Psychomachia. Placed by Cathedral Square.

h-victor.name: Victor’s hidden havens
h-victor.html: Several havens, all well hidden in wealthy districts. One is placed among the Lake Drive mansions of Shorewood, just past the last Kindred patrol. After Victor’s death the Chapel cleaned out his havens, but not all of them: who knows what Vienna papers still sit in the safes.

h-mortius.name: Dr. Mortius’s haunted house
h-mortius.html: Protected by the forbidden Haunted House ritual: mortals whisper that it is haunted and keep away. His ghoul retainers die often defending him from Lupines. He does not like to be disturbed.

h-hrothulf.name: Hrothulf’s house
h-hrothulf.html: A modest two-storey suburban home “solidly in the Outlands,” its neighbours demolished for yard space. The door is patched over bullet holes from Gracis’s latest attack, and the basement vault is full of traps. The Lupine have learned to avoid it. Placed in Elm Grove, just past the Anubi line.
h-hrothulf.src: Milwaukee by Night, Hrothulf p. 57; Scene 17 p. 112

h-badr.name: Badr-al-Budur’s condominium
h-badr.html: A small condo near the University. She travels the Northwest on contracts but always comes back here. Anarchs hire her to kill Elders, Elders hire her to kill Anarchs, and with the Prince dead business is about to boom.

h-decker.name: Decker’s motel
h-decker.html: Decker keeps no regular haven, fearing the Lupine would find it. For now he sleeps in the windowless bathroom of a cheap motel near the Outlands, with Julia Calvin beside him. Placed on 76th St just below Good Hope Road, on his own patrol line.
h-decker.src: Milwaukee by Night, Decker p. 37; Julia p. 39

h-thomas.name: Thomas’s borrowed bedrooms
h-thomas.html: He stays with rich teenage girls from Outlands high schools whenever their parents are travelling. Placed around Fox Point and River Hills.

h-milo.name: The lakeshore drains
h-milo.html: Milo never sleeps in the same place twice. In a drain pipe down by the lake, something chased him and told him it would eat every Kindred in the city, one by one. Nobody believes him. Placed at a storm outfall below the North Point bluff.

parkcounty.name: Milwaukee County Stadium
parkcounty.html: Crowds big enough to hide enemies from one another make fights rare. Lucina and Hrothulf hold season box seats; the Anarchs sit in the bleachers.

sprecher.name: Sprecher Brewery
sprecher.html: After a good game the Blood Brothers walk in past a guard they have Dominated into submission and party until dawn, bringing their own music and lighting. The fermenting wort smells wonderful to the dead.

zoo.name: Milwaukee County Zoo
zoo.html: Not official Elysium, but the Kindred have agreed not to fight here. Even Elders come in the early hours to see the animals. Anarchs dare each other to sample the most disgusting blood on offer (water buffalo, for instance).

medical.name: Milwaukee Regional Medical Complex
medical.html: Anarchs sneak into the refrigerated blood bank just after the night’s emergency supplies are drawn, giggling as they feast. Rumour says one Council member keeps a haven in the complex’s upper offices.

wmpark.name: West Milwaukee Park
wmpark.html: Where Kindred party, and where enemies meet safely. On the rare nights Elders must parley with Anarchs, they do it here. Several failed peace talks between Lucina and Akawa took place here, Akawa hidden and speaking through a Blood Brother. Ken Elliot’s, Country Gardens and Grenadier’s are close by.

southgate.name: Southgate Shopping Mall
southgate.html: Open until midnight on weekends and patrolled by enough security, bought with Elder strings, to keep Anarchs out. Expensive boutiques survive almost entirely on Elder custom, and some Elders hold business meetings in its corridors.

hilton.name: Airport Hilton
hilton.html: Visiting dignitaries and Camarilla officials are lodged here, supposedly for the fine rooms and an easy departure. In truth the Council fears the Anarchs would risk attacking a visitor downtown, and guests are easier to watch out here, far from anything worth hiding.

mitchell.name: General Mitchell International
mitchell.html: A short midnight hop from Chicago is the safest way in. Council members meet visiting dignitaries here, while Gracis’s spies log every arrival. Parovich’s network, which did the same, is being checked and purged since his exposure, and not all of its people have been found.

timmerman.name: Lawrence J. Timmerman Airport
timmerman.html: Almost opposite Mitchell and dangerously close to the Outlands, so few Kindred use it, which means few watch it. Anarchs pick up friends and new allies here, and quietly, some Elders do too.

amtrak.name: Milwaukee Road depot (Amtrak)
amtrak.html: The railways are largely run by the Kindred of Chicago. For money or a large favour, sealed cars carry Vampires through Lupine country unseen and unsmelled.

port.name: Port of Milwaukee
port.html: Sea travel is safe from Lupines but slow, and a Vampire must stay out of the sun for days. Few use it, which is why it’s the cleverest way in. Decker would need someone else to watch the ports if he ever sealed the city.

fair.name: State Fair Park
fair.html: Marked deep in Blood Brother country on the War Map. Its empty grounds and barns make a quiet off-season rumble site.

graceland.name: Graceland Cemetery
graceland.html: Just south of Good Hope, one of the famous dueling grounds where Elders settled scores in the early 1900s. Now it is too far from downtown and too close to the Anarchs for Elders to risk. The Anarchs have taken up the custom, mostly stake fights, and study every headstone so they know the terrain.

army.name: U.S. Army Reserve Center
army.html: Merik declared it off limits, and whoever rules next will likely keep it that way. The F.B.I. has run operations from here for months. Nobody knows whether they know about Vampires, and nobody wants to help them find out. Fences, wire and guards deter the curious.

jungleman.name: Jungleman
jungleman.html: A small dance bar on West Townsend Street beside Wanderers Rest, owned by a powerful ghoul called Vrasks. He will kill anybody (or so he claims) in exchange for Vampiric blood, and buys blood from broke Anarchs. His original master may still be in the city, quietly backing him.

mountmary.name: Mount Mary College
mountmary.html: Source of the Church of Isis, a feminist nature cult with seven or eight genuinely sensitive witches. Dr. Mortius secretly uses them to sweep the city for the anomaly without risking himself; the other Tremere would be appalled. Rumour ties the order to the Lupine: they take frequent trips into the wilds. (The book puts the college “just east” of Jungleman; the real campus lies to the west.)

brynwood.name: Brynwood Country Club
brynwood.html: One of the largest clubs lining Good Hope Road. Its fairways and tree lines give Lupines the advantage they enjoy in the woods.

tripoli.name: Tripoli Country Club
tripoli.html: The other great club on Good Hope. Anarchs “doing Good Hope” floor it past here.

joanarc.name: St. Joan of Arc Chapel
joanarc.html: In the 1960s a mighty Magus had this medieval chapel moved stone by stone to the centre of the null zone so he could study it. Lupines killed him, but the chapel still stands over the spot where Usla buried the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote, reshaped as his own hand and left eye. Whoever recovers them becomes nearly unbeatable and is hunted by every Lupine alive.
joanarc.src: Milwaukee by Night, History p. 13; Downtown map #10

marquette.name: Marquette University
marquette.html: A few harmless cults, a Society of Leopold member on the faculty, and the central plaza where the anomaly peaks. It is not truly dead: there is too much magic here, and it drowns out spells. Tremere, Lupines and Anarchs all prowl the campus.

sinai.name: Mount Sinai Medical Center
sinai.sub: Northern edge of the null zone
sinai.html: The anomaly reaches north past the hospital.

childrens.name: Old Children’s Hospital
childrens.sub: Western edge of the null zone
childrens.html: The book uses Children’s Hospital as the zone’s western limit; it is marked at the hospital’s old Wisconsin Avenue site.

foresthome.name: Forest Home Cemetery
foresthome.html: The dueling grounds of the 1901–06 Elder war are “scattered across the city,” usually cemeteries isolated enough that friends can’t hide nearby and police can be steered away. Forest Home, the grandest Victorian cemetery in town, is assigned as one. The Graves, a minor Caitiff gang, haunt it.
foresthome.src: Milwaukee by Night, History p. 14 (“scattered across the city”)

calvary.name: Calvary Cemetery
calvary.html: A hilltop cemetery above Bluemound Road, assigned as a dueling ground. Scott and Akawa have nearly killed each other more than once; Kindred lay bets on the next bout.

g-scorpions.name: Scorpions turf
g-scorpions.html: A dangerous, violent little mortal gang right next to Blood Brother territory. They jeer at strangers at red lights but won’t attack unless provoked.
g-scorpions.src: Milwaukee by Night, War of Tribes p. 87

g-disp.name: The Dispossessed
g-disp.html: One of the minor Caitiff gangs that Gracis, Lucina and Parovich are courting as a counterweight to Akawa. Placed in the Menomonee Valley rail yards.

g-dark.name: The Darkboys
g-dark.html: A small Caitiff crew that is no threat to Akawa yet. Placed around Clarke Square on the near south side.

g-war.name: Warlords
g-war.html: One Vampire and four ghouls. Placed along Teutonia Avenue on the north side.

lup-cave.name: The Mouse pack’s cave
lup-cave.html: Off a dark stretch of Route 43 north, Lupines riddled the Mask’s car with machine-gun fire and threw the party into a cave with a three-foot entrance. At the back lay the fresh remains of the Justicar who was supposed to investigate the murders. Horatio’s Coyote broke the Mouse pack’s hold and let the Mask go. Placed in the Milwaukee River ravines near Mequon.
lup-cave.src: Milwaukee by Night, A Midnight Moon pp. 99–106

lup-coyote.name: Coyote rendezvous
lup-coyote.html: Horatio is planning even when he seems to be talking. His pack is Red Talons, wolves to the bone, with exactly as much humanity as the job requires. All he needs is the Kindred distracted long enough to hold Marquette and dig. Placed in the quarry country past Menomonee Falls.

lup-eagle.name: Eagle staging ground
lup-eagle.html: The Eagle pack is almost entirely Wendigo. If the Anubi falter even once, the Eagle will push into the inner city; three or four would reach it and die there, but Kindred losses would be severe. The pack has people among the city’s Native Americans and a secret property, the Seven Fires casino. This autumn the blighted woods keep them home. Placed in the Root River woods of Franklin.

lup-usla.name: Where Usla went into the lake
lup-usla.html: After burying the totems, the dying Usla crawled into the waters of Lake Michigan and was never seen again. Lupines have converged on the area ever since without knowing why.

hist-1674.name: Manhanawaukee-Seepe
hist-1674.html: Père Marquette’s party visited the tribal gathering place at the rivers’ meeting. Among them was the scout “Petre Dubois”, who vanished every dawn. He was Hrothulf, a Dane Embraced in 5th-century Britain, who married into the Chippewa and later Embraced his wife Chiclena.

hist-juneau.name: Juneautown (1818)
hist-juneau.html: Solomon Juneau’s settlement east of the river. Hrothulf moved in early, dominated its leaders and became its Prince, drawing French Kindred down from Canada.

hist-kilbourn.name: Kilbourntown (1834)
hist-kilbourn.html: Byron Kilbourn’s town west of the river already had a Prince: Gracis Nostinus, Hrothulf’s blood-brother and sworn enemy. Their war of assassins left almost every other local Kindred dead by 1840. Kilbourntown even aimed a loaded cannon across the river at Juneautown, though it never fired.

hist-1900.name: New Year’s Eve, 1900
hist-1900.html: The border watch failed, which has never been explained. Lupines got deep into the city and Prince Erik Pointene died defending his palace. Terence Merik led the counter-attack that saved Kindred Milwaukee and made his name. The palace site is not given; this marker is symbolic.

ps-house.name: Ruins of Merik’s hilltop house
ps-house.sub: Where the Prince met Final Death
ps-house.html: A once-lovely house “on a hill… on the very edge of the Milwaukee Outlands”, with a basement dungeon where Merik drugged and chained the Mask and held Lt. Wilks. It burned during the final battle, and Wilks ran to meet the fire trucks, keeping his silence. Placed on the bluffs above the Menomonee River Parkway.
ps-house.src: Milwaukee by Night, Dreams of Madness pp. 118–123

ps-roof.name: Lisa Urgen’s rooftop trap
ps-roof.html: After a chase across a boardwalk and through a gutted brick shell, the Inquisitor locked the Mask on the roof of an abandoned lakeside hotel (fish wallpaper, carved dolphins) with a flamethrower and ten minutes until sunrise. Placed on the Bay View lakefront.
ps-roof.src: Milwaukee by Night, War of Tribes pp. 95–96

ps-lot.name: The abandoned factory lot
ps-lot.html: After fleeing the police, the Blood Brothers stopped behind an abandoned factory, where the Prince’s Dominated Union struck: motorcycle jousts among broken glass. Placed in the Menomonee Valley.
ps-lot.src: Milwaukee by Night, War of Tribes p. 88

ps-scene.name: Fresh murder scene
ps-scene.html: Merik’s drained victims were left where they would be found, and the Journal printed it on the front page. At the second scene the Mask spotted a Lupine slipping away to report to the Union. Placed near Brady Street.

f-hearth.name: The Last Hearth storefront
f-hearth.sub: Marta’s alterations shop, near Mitchell Street
f-hearth.html: A rented storefront where Marta takes in alterations and cooks community suppers. To the street it is a cluttered tailoring counter with a back kitchen. The absentee landlord is weighing a better-paying tenant; he is an ordinary man, not anyone’s pawn. Most months the Spare Chair Supper is held here.

f-counter.name: Juneau Avenue bascule bridge
f-counter.html: The supplement leaves the bridge open, so this map uses the Juneau Avenue crossing. That is the old Chestnut Street site where the 1845 Bridge War broke the city in two, which suits a refuge whose road still demands a white flag. City bridge tenders do their ordinary work; Oren’s refuge occupies a small private threshold beside the machinery.
f-counter.src: Unclaimed City p. 9, 19 (bridge chosen for play)

f-shop.name: Leon’s repair shop
f-shop.sub: A rented bay in the Menomonee Valley
f-shop.html: Audio gear and industrial controls on the benches, a tram prototype under a tarp, and a brass dog that is not his. It counts as a place of power only while people are inventing; it is not a freehold.

f-hall.name: Riverwest practice hall
f-hall.sub: Where the Standing Ovation opens most reliably
f-hall.html: A fictional neighbourhood hall with folding chairs, a piano missing two keys, and the best acoustics Nina can afford. She has cancelled two rehearsals here since the applause started continuing after the room emptied.

f-pabst.name: 100 East Wisconsin
f-pabst.html: A new office tower, completed in 1989, stands where the Pabst Building rose over the old city. There are no accessible ruins here. Everything that survived of the Hall of the Copper Hart survives only in the Dreaming, where the Unbuilt Stair still begins.

f-domes.name: Mitchell Park Domes
f-domes.html: Three glass domes holding a rain forest, a desert and a seasonal show garden through the Wisconsin winter. Arthur Saye works here and draws impossible gardens on the backs of discarded forms.

f-celia.name: Celia’s rented room
f-celia.sub: Beginner cello lessons, Lower East Side
f-celia.html: A second-floor room with a music stand, a patched coat on the door and a letter to her sponsor she keeps not posting. The rent now comes out of the last of her savings.

f-ruth.name: Ruth’s kitchen table
f-ruth.html: Bus schedules under a glass tabletop, a road atlas worn soft, and coffee for anyone who wants to argue about the best way to a real destination. Ruth runs courier and driving jobs from the phone on the wall.

f-kit.name: Kinnickinnic Avenue junk shops
f-kit.html: Secondhand stores and Saturday tables where abandoned futures are sold cheap: an instrument after two bad lessons, a half-sewn costume, a child’s outdated map. Kit’s bicycle is usually chained outside, freshly repaired by Oren.

f-bjorn.name: Inner Harbor docks
f-bjorn.html: Irregular dockside work and repairs. Bjorn keeps the only locally known working scale-light lantern in a locker here, wrapped in a fisherman’s sweater.

f-ivory.name: Ivory’s high school
f-ivory.html: Bells, hall passes and assignments with a comprehensible end. Here Ivory is just a grumpy schoolgirl: she dislikes the place and leans on its routine to stay steady. Some classmates and teachers are worth knowing. None of them suspects that the girl in the back row is the last overseer of the Michigan Pocket. Placed at a north-side public high school.

f-lola.name: Lola Wendt’s apartment
f-lola.sub: Playbills, newsletters, and a leaking basement
f-lola.html: An ordinary apartment whose value is its records. Lola holds a duplicated 1980 supper invitation that puts two supposedly unrelated war incidents on the same night. Right now she mostly needs boxes and two people with a car.

f-eddie.name: Eddie Rusk’s ghost club
f-eddie.sub: Back room of a south-side bowling alley
f-eddie.html: A small amateur group that investigates hauntings over pitchers of beer. A newer member has started publishing names and addresses without consent, and Eddie has to choose between the club and the people it says it protects.

f-warren.name: A door left unforced
f-warren.sub: Mortal approach to the Low Candle Way
f-warren.html: A service door under the Wisconsin Avenue bridge leads into the old Nosferatu warrens. The old shared work of sluagh and Nosferatu in the Michigan Pocket ended when Parovich went over to the Sabbat; Ivory’s arrangement with individual Nosferatu may now be no bigger than this door staying unforced. Being seen here exposes someone’s movements; it does not give the observer a road into the Keep.

c-jade-floor.name: Jade Riley’s floor
c-jade-floor.sub: A whole storey of an office tower on East Michigan Street
c-jade-floor.html: The new Brujah Primogen’s official haven: the entire twentieth floor of a glass tower, bought through a shell company of her grandsire’s. A library, a gym, and a reception hall where nobody has yet been received. The floor stands empty for now. After the fight with Dragos, Jade moved to her reserve haven, and the lights up here run on timers.

c-macy-house.name: Macy Carver’s house
c-macy-house.html: A small suburban house with peeling blue paint, bought with Macy’s trust fund. Protest posters, stacks of zines, and a windowless basement behind a reinforced door. The Brujah Primogen sleeps here now. The house is inside the Anubi patrol zone, and Decker knows exactly who is staying in it.

c-rusty.name: The Rusty Nail
c-rusty.sub: Punk basement where Jamie Robinson sings
c-rusty.html: A cramped Riverwest basement: sticky floor, a home-built stage and the best sound in town. Jamie Robinson’s band, the Rust Saints, plays here, and Macy finds half her counterculture contacts in the crowd. Union Anarchs and Blood Brothers come to the same shows and pretend not to see each other.

c-gas-lot.name: The lot where the gas station stood
c-gas-lot.sub: The Robinson family station on Highway 41
c-gas-lot.html: For thirty years the Robinson family’s gas station stood here, on the road out of the city, until it was condemned for a highway widening. One morning the demolition crew found a level, empty pad: no foundations, no pumps, no fuel stains. Ivory had taken it to the Michigan Pocket. Jamie knows where it went and doesn’t know how he feels about it.

c-chapel.name: The Chapel
c-chapel.sub: Tremere chantry · a brewer’s mansion on Highland Boulevard
c-chapel.html: An old beer baron’s mansion on “Sauerkraut Boulevard”, a few blocks west of the null zone’s edge. The chantry’s researchers work and sleep here. Since Victor’s death the link to Vienna is a formality, and the Chapel draws on unorthodox resources more freely every week. Luke Newman runs security for now.

c-victor-death.name: The Chapel’s east wing
c-victor-death.html: Drake of the Mouse pack, already twisted by the Wyrm, walked through the wards as if they weren’t there and killed Vienna’s watchdog in his own laboratory. The wing is sealed. Newman has rebuilt the defences and won’t say what let Drake in.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The wards were weakened from the inside. Jesselin found a way in through Haberman’s social correspondence and slipped Drake the “key”.

c-isis.name: Temple of the Church of Isis
c-isis.sub: An esoteric church on Brady Street
c-isis.html: Above an incense shop: a room with blue walls, sistrums, and a copy of Isis nursing Horus. To its congregation it is a neo-Egyptian fellowship with Thursday meditations. The inner circle drinks blood and keeps the Chapel’s secrets. Two of that circle, Kayla and Arianna, are ghouls. The book places the church’s witches at Mount Mary College; this is its city temple.

c-uwm.name: University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee
c-uwm.sub: Where Arianna studies and Doctor Fire teaches
c-uwm.html: The campus in the city’s north-east corner. Arianna studies Egyptology here and runs between lectures and the Chapel. One floor down, in the archaeology department, teaches the professor the hunters call Doctor Fire.

c-711.name: The empty corner
c-711.html: Annalena stopped here while fleeing the Gloaming Keep, and that was the last thing that ever happened to the store. By morning the corner was a weedy lot that looked untouched for decades. The Mists have wiped the store from nearly everyone’s memory. Nearly: a former night clerk comes back here every night without knowing why, a couple of cab drivers have an address in their logs that doesn’t exist, and a soda distributor keeps billing a customer nobody can find.

c-warehouses.name: The railside warehouses
c-warehouses.html: Rusting sheds between the railroad and the meatpacking plant. Dragos Dalca marched his spawn out of here, and from here he began his chase of a Camarilla team in dragon form. Behind Warehouse No. 7, a ramp wide enough for a truck leads down into the underground, hidden by little more than a wall.

c-breach1.name: Masquerade breach No. 1
c-breach1.sub: A dragon on the late news
c-breach1.html: A late-news crew filming a car crash on Kinnickinnic Avenue caught something huge, winged and scaled chasing three running figures over the rooftops. The tape aired once. The Nosferatu and Gracis’s people are still hunting down copies, and “the Milwaukee Dragon” has become an urban legend and a talk-radio staple.

c-breach2.name: Masquerade breach No. 2 · the fish plant
c-breach2.html: Dragos took his material here: off the conveyors, and from the homeless his servants trucked in from under the viaducts. Here Jade Riley killed him with her hands in the middle of the whole Camarilla’s battle with his creatures. Fire, hundreds of witnesses on the neighbouring piers, pieces of things that were neither fish nor human. Officially, an ammonia explosion. The plant is closed and still cordoned off.

c-viaduct.name: The camp under the viaduct
c-viaduct.html: Tents and barrel fires under the freeway. All autumn people vanished from here, two or three at a time, and nobody cared except the homeless themselves. They were taken to the fish plant. Some came back in a form nobody here talks about.

c-guillem-church.name: St. Jude’s, closed
c-guillem-church.html: A boarded-up Walker’s Point church from which Velez ran the infiltration: city maps on the sacristy walls, the stains of a Vaulderie in the altar. The Camarilla found it empty. Velez left a day before the raid; someone warned him.

c-guillem-boat.name: The yacht Santa Eulàlia
c-guillem-boat.html: A decommissioned yacht under a borrowed name at the McKinley moorings. The hold is blacked out, the portholes painted over from inside. Velez never spends more than two nights running here, and when he leaves he goes under the water, into the shadows.

c-maximus-shop.name: Charms & Needles
c-maximus-shop.sub: Maximus McKenzie’s tattoo parlour · Bay View
c-maximus-shop.html: A tattoo shop with a shelf of amulets. Through the back door Maximus sold blood-magic totems to Union Caitiff and Anarchs: wards, silencers, “luck in a fight”. Every piece was made with Sabbat blood and tied its owner to him a little. The shop is shut and the sign is gone, but some of the totems are still around their owners’ necks.

c-jesselin.name: A suite at the Pfister
c-jesselin.html: The city’s oldest grand hotel. On its top floor, under another name, lives Jesselin: charity evenings, opera invitations, lunch with a city councilman’s wife. A copper scrying bowl in the bathroom and a mirror draped in black velvet in the wardrobe.

c-ethan.name: Ethan Stone’s roost
c-ethan.sub: The roof of a grain elevator · Menomonee Valley
c-ethan.html: A concrete elevator above the valley. From its roof he has a clear shot over half of Blood Brother turf. Ethan keeps his bows here, bundles of arrows with different heads, and sleeps in an empty grain bin.

c-dominique.name: Dominique’s flat
c-dominique.html: The fourth floor of a shabby low-income block. This is where Dominique killed the Camarilla vampire who came to check on him, with a lighter and a can of air freshener. There is still a black scorch on the kitchen ceiling. The neighbours think a frying pan exploded.

c-gunther.name: Gunther’s boathouse
c-gunther.html: An old shed on the bank of the pond above the dam: upturned boats, nets, the smell of pipe smoke and wet fur. Gunther has lived on this water since the city was still Kilbourntown. Sometimes Mercer comes here, the last of the Mouse.

c-soraya.name: The house that isn’t there
c-soraya.html: A large old manor of chimneys, gables and ivy stands a few blocks from downtown, on a spot where no city map shows it. Passers-by turn aside before they reach the wall and don’t remember turning: a rare marriage of Dominate and Umbral mysticism that folds the house a few blocks “sideways” from the street. No electricity, no gas, no water mains; at night the windows burn with candles.

c-hunters.name: Wolfgang’s garage
c-hunters.sub: The hunters’ hideout and armoury · West Allis
c-hunters.html: A two-bay garage. Under a false floor in the inspection pit: stakes, jugs of gasoline, a crossbow, two Scandinavian-forged swords and a crate of Doctor Fire’s books. Pinned over the invoices on the corkboard is a map of the city’s havens, wrong in places and right in the worst ones. Sometimes someone leaves a dried flower on a car hood, or a child’s drawing with a hint in it. The hunters think they have a secret well-wisher. They’re right.

c-casino.name: Seven Fires Bingo & Casino
c-casino.sub: Secretly owned by the Eagle pack
c-casino.html: A loud hall of bingo and slot machines on the south side. The owners of record are Native American families of the city with whom the Eagle pack shares kinship, friendship and obligations. The real owner is the pack: the casino pays for lawyers and land, buys influence with community councils, and gives the Wendigo a place to meet people without leaving their own. (A fictional business; the real tribal casinos of 1991 Milwaukee have nothing to do with it.)

c-mercer.name: The telephone exchange
c-mercer.sub: Where Mercer works the night shift
c-mercer.html: A brick telephone-company building full of switching frames. Mercer, the last Garou of the Mouse pack, works here as a night technician and listens to the city down the wires.

c-blight.name: The blighted groves
c-blight.sub: Defiled places of power in the Root River woods
c-blight.html: Old sacred places in the woods that Maximus and Jesselin poisoned with Goratrix blood magic. The undergrowth is dying, the creeks smell of copper, and Banes crawl up out of the ground. The Eagle pack fights the infestation every night, which is exactly why it wasn’t watching the city when the Sabbat came in.

c-anchor-e.name: Anchor East · the North Point Water Tower
c-anchor-e.html: The Gothic water tower of 1873 above the bluff. Inside the shaft, ringed around the standpipe, the Chapel has mounted a coil of copper antennae under the lamp-room. The tower holds water, water holds reflections, and the lake is the biggest mirror in the city: this anchor “looks” at the null zone through water. The tower’s spire also stands on the Lake Park Truce’s ground, which the Garou would call a provocation if they knew.

c-anchor-s.name: Anchor South · the roof of the Hotel Warszawa
c-anchor-s.html: A tired old hotel with a neon crown on its roof. The antenna is dressed up as a TV aerial. From the roof you can see the dome of St. Josaphat’s, a basilica built from another city’s stones, and the Allen-Bradley clock the neighbourhood calls the Polish Moon: the anchor drinks from that “reassembled” holiness and from a clock that tells its own time.

c-anchor-w.name: Anchor West · the mound in the Root River woods
c-anchor-w.sub: Deep in the parkway forest, south-west
c-anchor-w.html: In a clearing among old oaks lies a slumped mound that appears in no survey. The antenna stands on a tripod wrapped in willow withies. The local Garou would call it a sacrilege if they found it, and they are fighting Banes a few miles south of it every night. The mound remembers the people who lived here before the city, and perhaps it remembers Usla.

c-anchor-n.name: Anchor North · the relay mast above Lincoln Creek
c-anchor-n.sub: A disused radio mast on the north side
c-anchor-n.html: An abandoned relay mast over the Lincoln Creek parkway. The Tremere hung a copper-wound antenna with sealed glyphs at its top. Mystically, the creek is a small thing that has refused to die: buried in culverts, it keeps resurfacing. The anchor borrows that stubbornness to keep the ring from collapsing.

c-ritual-core.name: The ritual’s target: expose the null zone
c-ritual-core.html: The four anchors are placed so their diagonals cross exactly over St. Joan of Arc Chapel. When all four are tuned, the ritual should “turn the null zone inside out” and show what keeps it dead. The Tremere think they will find a source. They don’t know that two halves of two totems lie under the chapel, which means the ritual will wake the Coyote and the Eagle at the same moment.

d-hearth.name: The Last Hearth
d-hearth.sub: Working freehold · a long brick bakehouse
d-hearth.html: A copper stove, a communal table, and cupboards labelled in generations of handwriting. The balefire lives in a shallow coal pan inside the stove. It grows on freely shared practical effort (teaching, repair, cooking, cleaning), so paying Marta to do everything does not feed it. Hospitality is hers to give, but a guest who takes a real share of the work can ask for one honest hearing before being refused. During a good supper the chimerical pantry may hold a remembered favourite dish. It cannot feed the neighbourhood for free.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: The landlord arrives while a chimerical kettle is shouting the name of someone who needs help. Marta needs one person to talk rent, one to silence the kettle and one to find the person. Everyone assumes she can do all three.

d-counter.name: The Counterweight
d-counter.sub: Working freehold · a gatehouse hung on chains
d-counter.html: A stone gatehouse suspended over a channel full of discarded destinations. Its balefire hangs in a bronze cage on the great weight that raises the dream-bridge, and sinks close to the dark water whenever the bridge opens. Inside: three pallets, an ironless tool cupboard, a shelf of thermoses. It welcomes travellers for a night. Oren’s door is valuable because it gives a dependable return from two otherwise unreliable routes.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: A stranded chimera presents a valid old admission token. Admitting it is possible. Protecting it from the passenger pursuing it will make tomorrow’s crossing uncertain. Oren asks for help; he does not announce a quest.

d-keep.name: The Gloaming Keep · outer court
d-keep.html: Broken Copper Hart architecture joined to the lower chambers of the dead sluagh households. The public story is that Ivory found an unclaimed ruin and made it habitable. The outer court has no sign of anything beyond it. Its reserve of Glamour is deeper than either public refuge, but almost all of it is committed, and it cannot be lent to the city without endangering what it protects. The Tremere alchemist Annalena recently got in uninvited; several of her ghouls never came out, and the roadside 7-Eleven where she stopped during her flight was erased by the fae as if it had never been.

d-wards.name: The private wards
d-wards.html: The eight presumed dead of 1981 are here, none of them sluagh. The collapsed refuge drifted out of step with earthly time, so they lived months of disordered confinement across five mortal years. Ivory gives regular care: observation, safe stretches of ordinary routine, personal anchors and carefully chosen contact. There is no automatic cure. She will not accept death and reincarnation as a treatment. Bjorn has noticed signs of more inhabitants but has not breached the wards. No route on this map is a back door here.

d-index.name: The Unfinished Index
d-index.html: Bookshelves drift through a great vaulted gulf; desks hang at odd angles and lamps swing from chains fixed to nothing. Shelves drift toward related questions, so to travel upward you ask a harder question; climbing harder doesn’t help. Half-written letters nest under the desks like swallows. It holds interrupted investigations, unpublished local writing, rejected civic schemes and forgotten marginalia. It is neither omniscient nor a machine for true names or cures. A reader must honestly advance one abandoned task before borrowing another.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: Mrs. Quire is shelving unfinished lives as unfinished manuscripts. A neighbourhood carpenter dreams nightly of shelves being built around him, and his apprentice thinks the sketches he abandons each morning are an art project. They are a request for help that the Index keeps reformatting.

d-stacks.name: The inner stacks
d-stacks.html: Somewhere in here are the original wording of Oren’s oath, a repair diagram that could make Leon’s tram run without the Glass, and Alisande’s unfinished speech proposing reforms to her own court. Each is a specific document someone has to find and interpret. None proves its author’s plan would have worked.

d-ward.name: The Crownless Ward
d-ward.sub: Overgrown towers, blue-lit windows, perpetual late afternoon
d-ward.html: A composite realm made from dreams of demolished buildings, old downtown ambitions, and projects whose promised inhabitants never came. Vines curtain carved walls, stairs stay aligned to floors that are gone, and three blocks can take you through a vanished hotel, a factory stairwell and an unrealized council chamber without a visible join. Each blue window holds a place somebody might still make. A window goes dark when its room is stripped or declared worthless, and brightens when someone starts an equivalent project in the waking city.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: The Surveyor of Necessary Losses offers to make one building safe in exchange for the permanent destruction of three others. Saving every tower is beyond nine people.

d-ruins.name: The distant ruins
d-ruins.sub: Where the Ward forgets its address
d-ruins.html: The Ward thins out into towers with no earthly echo at all: civic projects announced and never built, and housing promised to people who were moved somewhere else first. The blue windows here are few and very bright. Improvised for this map.

d-seat.name: The Far Guest’s Seat
d-seat.sub: A black mountain on the starlit lake
d-seat.html: There is no earthly island here. In the Near Dreaming a black blade of rock rises through water bright with impossible constellations, its reflection sometimes meeting the real peak halfway up. The dragon that lived here departed Earth long ago. Nothing sleeps under the floor and nothing is waiting to wake. The lair rewards journeys freely undertaken and resists commands laid on someone else’s journey. Its apparent distance changes; do not plot it on a mortal chart.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: The mountain has begun accepting petitions in the absent dragon’s name. It cannot grant them, and each unanswered one adds a step to the Listening Stair and lengthens the road home.

d-arrivals.name: Hall of Arrivals
d-arrivals.html: Stone niches sized for gifts, some for givers far larger than people. What remains of the hoard is here: a bell frame with no bell, navigation tools, jars of unfamiliar seeds and gifts whose meanings are lost. The gold and the great weapons left with their owner.

d-stair.name: The Listening Stair
d-stair.sub: Repeats your purpose back to you
d-stair.html: It repeats a visitor’s declared purpose until they can tell it apart from someone else’s expectations. It is getting longer: one step for every petition the mountain cannot answer.

d-winter.name: The Winter Orchard
d-winter.html: Pale fruit ripens in warm snow. The last of it, the Fruit That Has No Name, is said to ripen only for someone who has found a hunger they cannot name. Bjorn wants it.

d-departure.name: The Departure Room
d-departure.html: A balcony over the route the Far Guest used to leave. The road is severed and cannot be followed.

d-orchard.name: The Glass Orchard
d-orchard.sub: Seasonal glade · three vast glass fruits
d-orchard.html: A rain forest, a desert, and a garden whose seasons turn around a single path, each sealed in a glass fruit. Human curiosity sustains it more reliably than any gardener. Force everything to bloom at once and you get spectacular colour, then an exhausted silence. Bjorn visits for flavours; Nina brings collaborators who need to want something again.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: Dream-seeds carried back from the mountain are sprouting among ordinary ambitions. People sketch houses that could only stand underwater, or rehearse music that needs a voice they don’t have. The problem is excess and fit, not hidden evil.

d-third.name: The Third Shift
d-third.sub: Workshop realm · the factory after the foreman leaves
d-third.html: Lathes sing counterpoint, chalk equations walk between benches, and small brass creatures carry scraps to projects that might need them. Its productive hours are limited. If nobody rests, the benches lengthen, the exit backs away, and a whole night vanishes into “one more adjustment.”

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: The Line That Might Have Been has acquired an immaculate timetable that nobody wrote. Its last stop is called COMPLETION, and Ruth insists no working transit system has a stop by that name.

d-ovation.name: The Standing Ovation
d-ovation.html: A shallow wooden stage facing audiences who nearly came: absent parents, future admirers, figures borrowed from the performer’s assumptions. They cannot tell you anything reliable about the real people whose faces they wear. Repeating a familiar success makes the exit curtains heavier; new, awkward work opens them.

d-wolfeye.name: The Country of the Wolf’s Eye
d-wolfeye.sub: Border distortion over the Marquette zone
d-wolfeye.html: Not empty but overfull. Shadows choose different directions, animals carved in stone seem to be paying attention, and a small cantrip may pick up an unintended audience. The buried Lupine relics remain the explanation, and the Silver Path grants no ownership of what lies beneath. Ruth goes around it. Leon wants to study the interference for his tram, and Oren says his test site isn’t nearly remote enough.

notes.title: The live problem
notes.html: One of Hester Ames’s notebooks has been lost at the edge of the zone. It is a small rescue with an uncertain supernatural witness, not an invitation to dig.

d-borrowed.name: Hall of Borrowed Voices
d-borrowed.html: A chamber Celia wants to relight as a public rehearsal and meeting hall open to every kith and court. It is not yet a working freehold.

d-foundry.name: The West Foundry
d-foundry.html: Cold furnaces and patient machinery. Miss Tuesday found the tram’s missing component here; negotiating for it means dealing with the Rent Collector.

d-bedrooms.name: The House with Enough Bedrooms
d-bedrooms.html: A many-storeyed house whose occupants have to agree together who stays. Somebody always wants one more room.

d-blueroom.name: Kit’s blue-lit room
d-blueroom.html: Kit holds a claim ticket for this room. It names them custodian, not owner, and they have been pretending not to understand the difference. Kit has promised it to a frightened newcomer chimera.

d-platform.name: The Waiting Platform
d-platform.sub: Echo of the demolished Everett Street depot
d-platform.html: An abandoned intercity dream-station at the outer edge of the Ward, placed here at the reflection of the old Milwaukee Road depot. The departure board shows emotionally persuasive trains that cannot carry a living traveller home. The old road toward Chicago ends here, and every departing train is named for someone who abandoned Milwaukee. Ruth is trying to secure a real host at the far end and test one short outward section.
d-platform.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, pp. 9, 23; improv placement

d-lanternthreshold.name: The Lantern Wake landing
d-lanternthreshold.html: Where the scale-light lantern is kindled and the enchanted boat pushes off. Placed in the lee of the McKinley Marina breakwater. Save one full charge for the way home.
d-lanternthreshold.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22; improv placement

d-pabstecho.name: The Copper Hart’s stair-foot
d-pabstecho.html: The Unbuilt Stair begins here. The antlered weathercock of the old Hall still turns on a spire that is not there, a stag climbing above the smoke.

d-eastecho.name: Eastern downtown echoes
d-eastecho.sub: Far bank of the White Flag Crossing
d-eastecho.html: Juneautown as it remembers itself: gaslit storefronts and a riverbank still disputing which side is the real Milwaukee.

c-quire.name: Mrs. Quire
c-quire.html: Built from card-catalogue drawers and ink-dark lace. She speaks softly because a shouted question rearranges whole wings.

c-rent.name: The Rent Collector
c-rent.html: Coat of old leases, a key for a tongue, bells in its cuffs. It knocks before entering even where there is no longer a wall.

c-surveyor.name: The Surveyor of Necessary Losses
c-surveyor.html: Rolled plans under one arm and a measuring chain that is always slightly too short.

c-tollman.name: The Tollman of Two Banks
c-tollman.html: Two incompatible uniforms stitched down the middle; each half insists it belongs to the lawful city.

c-usher.name: The Ashen Usher
c-usher.html: Overlapping flakes like cooled ash and a coal for a mouth. Its shadow keeps wings its body never had.

c-tuesday.name: Miss Tuesday
c-tuesday.html: A long-legged workshop dog of gauges and rivets. She follows Leon without belonging to him.

c-encore.name: The Encore
c-encore.html: Footlights with nobody between them; applause without hands.

c-swifts.name: Glasshouse swifts
c-swifts.html: They help Arthur Saye tend the Orchard and dart between the three glass fruits faster than the eye can follow.

c-whale.name: The copper whale
c-whale.html: A small copper whale dreamed into the Third Shift by a brewery worker. It feeds on steam and gets furious when called a fish.

c-knock.name: The Knock-under-the-Bridge
c-knock.html: An invented urban-legend creature Ivory uses on young Hunters, placed under the Holton Street viaduct. Her exercises have controlled ground, escape routes and an abort signal she enforces. The danger is a trainee assuming an unrelated encounter follows the same rules.

c-coat.name: The Coat on the Last Bus
c-coat.sub: Ivory’s training chimera · rides the route
c-coat.html: An empty coat riding the last eastbound run along Wisconsin Avenue, always one seat ahead of you.

c-lantern.name: The Lantern in the Drain
c-lantern.html: A swinging light deep in a lakeshore storm drain. Placed near the outfall where Milo swears something woke and spoke to him. Ivory’s lantern is a tame exercise. Whatever Milo met is not, and a Hunter who can’t tell them apart is exactly the trainee she worries about.

c-staircase.name: A staircase of people
c-staircase.sub: County Stadium on a good night
c-staircase.html: Now and then a crowd making room for a stranger to see produces a brief chimerical staircase. It has nothing to do with which supernatural faction owns the seats.

w-ribbon.name: June’s mended ribbon
w-ribbon.sub: Found outside the Keep’s outer approach
w-ribbon.html: Carried out with discarded fabric. Marta recognises it: she made it for June before the war. It proves an old object survived, not that eight people did.

t-bell.name: The Bell of the Last Transfer
t-bell.html: Once repaired, it can call a stranded admitted passenger back to the last legitimate stop on that one restored route, if they hold a valid punched ticket and can hear and answer. It cannot recover the dead or overrule a closed freehold. Wired to the Glass shard, it is a hazard: it sometimes rings for passengers nobody can see.

t-glass.name: A shard of the Glass of the Second Door
t-glass.html: Leon bought it as salvage without knowing what it was. The Glass once let its bearer contaminate prepared thresholds with convincing false escapes; it never gave unlimited control. The other pieces are unaccounted for. Destroying this one doesn’t kill anyone, collapse any freehold or cure anyone. Whether to keep it is an ethical question, not a hidden campaign objective.

t-key.name: The Key of a Borrowed Room
t-key.html: Opens one unoccupied, unclaimed room in the Ward for a night. The guest must leave a practical improvement behind. Use it without improving anything and the Rent Collector comes.

t-thimble.name: Marta’s Mending Thimble
t-thimble.html: A garment mended patiently for a willing person can carry one vivid comforting memory into an enchanted experience: a personal anchor, not a cure. Marta refuses commissions made without the wearer’s knowledge.

t-pennant.name: The White Pennant
t-pennant.html: Guarantees that the Tollman hears the bearer out before refusing the crossing, provided their peaceful purpose is declared honestly. It guarantees a hearing, not agreement or safety.

t-lamp.name: The Scale-Light Lantern
t-lamp.html: A lamp with a translucent dragon-scale shutter. It reveals the Lantern Wake and a small circle of reliable water. Each charge comes from completing a journey freely promised to another person. The Usher knows it as a loan from an older visitor and wants the terms renewed.

t-fruit.name: The Fruit That Has No Name
t-fruit.html: Shared willingly by two people, it lets each convey one sensation the other has never known. Eaten alone it has no flavour, which Bjorn has not yet worked out.

s-citadel.name: The Exposition Hall
s-citadel.sub: Citadel of the Hierarchy · relic of the 1881 Exposition Building
s-citadel.html: The great Industrial Exposition Building burned in 1905, and the Auditorium was raised on its ashes. In the Shadowlands the old hall still stands, all iron trusses and dusty bunting, and it is Milwaukee’s Citadel. Anacreon Konrad Vollmer keeps his court on the balcony where the 1881 opening speeches were made. Below him, in the living world, the Kindred Council whispers through Symphony nights. The Hierarchy has been listening for decades.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Reapers want Merik’s victims brought here before the Renegades of Bay View or the free wraiths of Walnut Street reach them. The Anacreon wants it done quietly, because the Chicago Necropolis has started asking why Milwaukee’s harvests run so thin.

s-citadel.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-pabst.name: The Pabst Building
s-pabst.html: Demolished ten years ago, the tower stands again on this side of the Shroud, ash-grey and whole, taller than anything around it. Hierarchy Monitors keep a lamp in the cupola to watch for Maelstrom weather over the lake. Nobody goes above the fourteenth floor. Doors there open onto stairwells that loop back on themselves, and the wraiths call it the False Floor.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The False Floor is what remains, on the death side, of the fae War of False Doors in 1981. The Glass of the Second Door scarred the relic as surely as it scarred the Dreaming. A sluagh might recognise the pattern. A Monitor never will.

s-pabst.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-plankinton.name: Plankinton House
s-plankinton.html: The grand hotel came down in 1980 to make room for the new Grand Avenue mall. Its relic lobby is the city’s market for soul-coin, favours and Stygian goods. Mr. Penny keeps the ledgers at the old front desk and charges a toll in memories for anything he cannot price in coin.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: A bundle of relic letters from the Third Ward fire of 1892 has come up for auction. Three separate wraiths claim the same grandmother wrote them.

s-plankinton.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-newhall.name: The Newhall House ruin
s-newhall.html: In January 1883 the Newhall House burned in the night and more than seventy people died. Many were servant girls trapped on the upper floors. The relic is a blackened shell that is always smouldering. Most of the dead moved on or were Reaped long ago. Something else has kept the fire going.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Every January the ruin flares. This year the smoke is drifting toward Old St. Mary’s, and the Inquisition cell in the basement has begun to dream of burning rooms.

s-newhall.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-depot.name: The Everett Street depot
s-depot.html: The Milwaukee Road’s great depot was torn down in 1965. Its relic platforms serve the Hearse Train, the Hierarchy’s overland line to the Chicago Necropolis. Harbingers ride it with sealed dispatches. In the Dreaming, the fae know the same spot as the Waiting Platform, and neither side has noticed the other yet.
s-depot.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-bronzeville.name: Walnut Street
s-bronzeville.sub: Relic Bronzeville · the free wraiths’ quarter
s-bronzeville.html: Milwaukee’s Black business and entertainment district along Walnut Street was cut apart by urban renewal and the North-South Freeway in the 1950s and ’60s. In the Shadowlands it is all still there: the barbershops, the churches, the clubs where the music ran till dawn. Its dead and its memories hold it together. Lorraine Hollis keeps the peace. The Hierarchy has no garrison here and has learned not to send one.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Lorraine is sheltering a newly dead woman the Reapers want. The woman hasn’t told anyone how she died, and her Shadow keeps answering for her.

s-bronzeville.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-soldiers.name: The Soldiers Home
s-soldiers.sub: Grim Legion garrison · Wood National Cemetery
s-soldiers.html: Veterans of four wars lie in the national cemetery around the old Soldiers Home. The Grim Legion, for those who died by violence, keeps its Milwaukee garrison in the relic barracks. Sergeant Reinholt drills them at dusk on a parade ground that the living know as lawn.
s-soldiers.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-forest.name: Forest Home chapel
s-forest.sub: The Pardoner’s seat · end of the Funeral Road
s-forest.html: The Victorian cemetery where Milwaukee’s brewers and mayors are buried. Its chapel is the Hierarchy’s registry of the dead, where every Reaped soul is entered in a book that is never quite finished. Father Anselm hears confessions here and pares Shadows back with Castigation.
s-forest.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-county.name: The County Grounds
s-county.html: For a century the county’s poor, insane and unclaimed were buried here in unmarked rows. In 1991 construction near the medical complex turned up the first graves, and archaeologists are now lifting them one by one. Every coffin raised breaks a Fetter. The Penitent Legion, keeper of those who died in madness and despair, is losing wraiths it has guarded for ninety years.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Matron Grau wants the excavation slowed. The living crew wants to finish by winter. A wraith who can make one archaeologist feel watched could buy her a week. The Anacreon has forbidden it.

s-county.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-baymill.name: The Rolling Mill
s-baymill.html: On 5 May 1886, striking workers marching for the eight-hour day were fired on by the state militia outside the Bay View rolling mills, and seven people died. The relic mill is a cold furnace hall where the Strikers’ Circle meets. They are Renegades who see the Hierarchy as one more set of owners. Joe Mazur leads them.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Circle wants Merik’s newly dead before the Reapers get them. Joe says it is to free them. The Anacreon says it is to recruit them. Both are partly right.

s-baymill.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-elgin.name: The Lady Elgin landing
s-elgin.html: On 8 September 1860 the excursion steamer Lady Elgin sank off the Illinois shore with roughly three hundred people aboard. Many were Third Ward Irish of Milwaukee’s Union Guard. Her relic still sails. The Emerald Legion, keeper of the accidentally dead, runs her as the ferry across the Sea of Shadows toward Chicago. She docks here at the harbor mouth on foggy nights.
s-elgin.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-police.name: The Broadway station
s-police.html: In November 1917 a bomb carried into the old Central Police Station exploded and killed nine officers and a civilian. Their relic station house still answers calls. The Ninth Watch, a squad sworn to the Grim Legion, walks a beat no living patrolman can see, and they are very interested in whoever has been draining people in Juneau Park.
s-police.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-joan.name: The Pyre Circle
s-joan.sub: Heretics · St. Joan of Arc Chapel
s-joan.html: Legend says one stone in the chapel is cold because Joan of Arc kissed it before she died. Sister Clotilde’s heretics believe it, and they believe Joan crossed over and passed beyond, into Transcendence. They gather around the stone to pray their way after her. Over the Marquette anomaly the Shroud behaves strangely, sometimes thick as felt and sometimes gone. Some nights their prayers seem to be answered.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: What answers is not Joan. It is the overabundance of magic around Usla’s buried totems, leaking through. The Circle’s “visions” are a Lupine relic dreaming.

s-forge.name: The Tannery Forge
s-forge.html: The valley’s old tanneries and packing houses left deep relics full of vats and hooks. Hilde Brauer’s Artificers forge Stygian steel, chains and soul-coin here for the Citadel. The smoke from the forge never quite leaves the valley.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: Hilde has quietly asked the Reapers to send her any wraith “too damaged to keep”. She has been told Merik’s victims may fit that description.

s-forge.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The underlying event or building is real history.

s-masquers.name: The Pabst Theater
s-masquers.html: The theatre is no relic, since it still stands in the living world, but the Shroud is thin in its gallery. Colette Duval’s Masquers rehearse there between living performances, learning the faces they will wear on errands for the Citadel.

s-bench.name: The bench in Juneau Park
s-bench.html: Merik’s frenzy began here: a couple kissing on a park bench on the way home from a movie. They woke on this side still holding hands, bound to the bench and to each other. They do not understand why the police tape is gone, or why the lake has turned grey.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Reapers, the Strikers’ Circle and Lorraine Hollis all want to reach them first, for different reasons. One of the couple is already listening to a voice that sounds exactly like her own.

s-four.name: The four from the headline
s-four.sub: Fetters scattered across the Lower East Side
s-four.html: “Vampire Murderer Kills Four.” Their bodies were left where they would be found. Their wraiths are less tidy. Each is Fettered to something different: a stairwell, a newspaper box, a borrowed coat, a voice on the WBIT late show. Two have already been Reaped. Two are hiding.

s-ashes.name: The burned house on the hill
s-ashes.html: Several of Merik’s ghouls died in the fire. Three woke in the Shadowlands still craving vitae that no longer exists for them. They prowl the relic of the house, which burns more completely on this side, and wait for the Prince to come home. He won’t. Destroyed Kindred leave no wraith, and nothing that was Merik has crossed.

s-hollow.name: The Interchange Hollow
s-hollow.html: The freeway interchange erased blocks of homes. In the Shadowlands the concrete courtyards between the ramps are open wounds: a Nihil spirals down past the Shroud into the Tempest. The Anarch rumbles fought here every month feed it a little. Wraiths cross the bridges above it quickly and do not look down.

s-drain.name: What Milo met
s-drain.html: Milo the Malkavian swears something in the drain pipes by the lake woke up, chased him, and promised to eat every Kindred in the city, one by one. Nobody believes him. He is right. A Spectre nests in the outfall: a Doppelganger whose Shadow devoured it decades ago, now fat on despair and drawn to the cold, borrowed lives of vampires. Ivory’s training chimera, the Lantern in the Drain, works just upstream. She has noticed the water tastes wrong.

s-tempest.name: The Sea of Shadows
s-tempest.html: Past the breakwaters the Shroud gives way to the Sea of Shadows, the lake’s death-side twin, rolling grey and endless under Maelstrom weather. The Lady Elgin crosses it. The Ice Road runs over it in winter. Everything else that sails it is hunting.

u-spire.name: The Spire of 100 East
u-spire.sub: Pattern-Spider nest over the lost Pabst
u-spire.html: The new glass tower is, in the Umbra, a single enormous crystal still being grown. Eight-Count, overseer of the downtown Pattern Spiders, nests at the top. Underneath lies the empty footprint of the old Pabst Building, the one place downtown the spiders won’t spin. The fae and the dead both have reasons for that. The spiders don’t.

u-tallest.name: The Tallest Thing
u-tallest.sub: Spirit of the city’s tallest tower
u-tallest.html: The great bank tower on East Wisconsin Avenue has the spirit of a proud civil servant. It is the tallest thing in the state and it knows it. It sees the whole Penumbra from its roof and will tell you what it sees for a compliment it has not heard before.

u-clockwork.name: The Clockwork Heart
u-clockwork.html: City Hall’s Umbral reflection is a ticking brass heart where Ledgerlings file the city’s permits and Weaver-clerks argue precedent. Since Merik died, the clerks have noticed someone is missing from the mayor’s strings, and they are deeply uneasy about who will pick them up.

u-inkwell.name: The Inkwell
u-inkwell.html: A spirit of news: ink-black, many-handed and always on deadline. It is mostly Weaver but has a Wyld streak for a good story. It trades rumours with spirits all over the city and printed the “Vampire Murderer” headline in the Umbra a full night before the mortal paper did.

u-static.name: Static
u-static.html: A crackling Bane that lives in the dispatch frequencies, feeding on panic and wrong addresses. It sent squad cars after the Mask during Psychomachia for the fun of it. Decker’s friendly patrolmen have noticed their radios go bad whenever Lupines are near.

u-coldrooms.name: The Cold Rooms
u-coldrooms.sub: MECCA and the Hyatt, where the Elders sleep
u-coldrooms.html: In the Umbra, vampires leave a stain. The rooms where the Elders sleep and meet show as voids: cold, grey and lightly Wyrm-tainted, where spirits refuse to go. Garou can read the Kindred’s whole downtown in this taint like a map. The Pattern Spiders spin around it and never through it.

u-skyweb.name: The Skywalk Web
u-skyweb.html: The skywalk is a great woven tube of Weaver silk in the Umbra, used by Weaver-messengers. A spirit can travel from the Hyatt to the Federal Plaza without touching the Penumbra floor.

u-wound.name: The Wound of Two Totems
u-wound.sub: Under St. Joan of Arc Chapel
u-wound.html: The buried hand and eye of Usla, once the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote, burn in the Penumbra like two coals in a split hearth. Spirits who come too close start to argue with themselves. Whoever lifts the relics will have the Wounded Eagle and Coyote’s Grin standing on either side of them, both demanding their piece back.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: Neither totem can take back its part alone, because Usla bound the two relics together when he shaped them into one body. Returning them takes Coyote and Eagle acting together, the one thing the two clans have not done in three hundred years.

u-stormcrows.name: The Storm-Crows
u-stormcrows.html: Small black spirits born from the storm itself. They fly in double flocks, one cawing for the Eagle and one for the Coyote, and will carry a message anywhere in the city for a mouthful of Gnosis. They always deliver it twice, once to each side.

u-eyewatch.name: The Eye in the Cloud
u-eyewatch.html: A vast amber eye opens in the clouds over the campus on overcast nights. It is the Coyote’s missing sight, looking for itself. Anyone it fixes on hears a joke in their own voice about something they have kept secret.

u-talonrake.name: The Raking Talon
u-talonrake.sub: The Eagle’s missing claw, in the storm
u-talonrake.html: On the south side of the storm, red light tears the sky in four parallel lines. It is the Talon clawing for its owner. Spirits that fly too high here come down in pieces.

u-mortiuswards.name: Mortius’s wards
u-mortiuswards.html: Dr. Mortius cannot reach the Umbra, but his Thaumaturgy leaves glyph-threads at the zone’s north edge to record what passes. Since Victor died and nobody from Vienna watches the Chapel, there are three times as many threads and the glyphs are darker. The Storm-Crows have learned to pull them, and soon one of them will pull the wrong one.

u-gambrinus.name: The Hall of Gambrinus
u-gambrinus.html: A smoky banqueting hall of carved oak and copper with the old king on his barrel-throne. Gambrinus is generous, sentimental and frightened: his brewery is losing money and he can feel it in his joints. He will trade almost anything for a reason to believe he will last.

u-copperqueen.name: The Copper Queen’s Court
u-copperqueen.sub: Spirit-queen of the State Street brewery
u-copperqueen.html: The busiest neutral ground in the city’s Umbra, a bright, roaring beer hall. Spirits of every allegiance drink side by side because nobody dares break the Queen’s peace. Garou of all three clans have been seen here on the same night, at different tables.

u-widow.name: The Widow of the Vats
u-widow.html: A tall, faded spirit in a copper-buttoned apron, polishing empty kettles. She knows every old recipe in Milwaukee and will give one away to anyone who promises to brew it somewhere.

u-upstart.name: The Upstart
u-upstart.sub: Spirit of the little Walker’s Point brewery
u-upstart.html: A young, cocky craft-brewery spirit, barely five years old, that thinks it can take on the giants. The Blood Brothers party in its hall, and it likes them. Gambrinus finds it charming. The Copper Queen hasn’t noticed it yet.

u-ironhorse.name: The Iron Horse
u-ironhorse.html: A thunder-voiced stallion of chrome and engine, its mane a plume of exhaust. It loves speed, loud men and open roads, and was proud that its children carried the Blood Brothers. It loved the wolf who rode with them. Akawa is gone now, and every night the Horse tears up and down the city’s avenues looking for him.

u-chromepack.name: The Chrome Pack
u-chromepack.html: A howling pack of motorcycle-spirits that run the Penumbra’s avenues at night. Garou Ragabash ride them for fun. Anyone who comes off can expect to be laughed at for a month.

u-tallow.name: Tallow
u-tallow.html: A slow, enormous Bane of fat and steam that seeps through the valley, reducing everything it touches into simpler, hungrier things. It is old, patient and very hard to kill, because the valley keeps feeding it.

u-tannin.name: The Tannin Pits
u-tannin.sub: Where hides were cured, and worse
u-tannin.html: Bubbling pits of black-brown liquor where the Tannin Twins, two Banes joined at the hip, cure anything thrown in until it can never rot or grow again.

u-herd.name: The Stockyard Herd
u-herd.html: Terrified herd-spirits, the memory of a century of animals driven to slaughter, stampeding through the smoke. Lupus-born Garou can’t stand to hear them. Lately something has been driving them out of the valley at dusk.

u-sabbatpact.name: Parovich’s legacy
u-sabbatpact.sub: The Sabbat’s remnants keep feeding the Wyrm
u-sabbatpact.html: Parovich learned what the rest of the Kindred never knew: the Banes of the Rendering will bargain. He fed blood to Gnaw, a rage-Bane, and Gnaw rode the Eagle’s raiders and made their raids wilder. Parovich was exposed and destroyed, but the bargain outlived him. The scattered remnants of Guillem Velez’s Sabbat found his old offerings and keep feeding Gnaw, no longer so that the Lupines break the city, but so that the Garou are too busy to look for Velez.

u-compost.name: Grandmother Compost
u-compost.html: An immense, unhurried spirit of rot and renewal, wrapped in steam and earthworms. She takes in the city’s filth and gives back green, and she is the only spirit the Wyrm, the Weaver and the Wyld all treat with respect. She has outlived three Garou septs and expects to outlive these.

u-foggate.name: The Fog Gate
u-foggate.sub: Where the lake fog comes ashore
u-foggate.html: At the harbor mouth the great lake fogs, the Grey Coming, enter the city’s Umbra like a slow army. Fog-spirits carry messages from Greatwater to anyone they find awake on the shore.

u-kkspirit.name: Kinnickinnic, in chains
u-kkspirit.html: A river spirit of muddy water and willow roots, bound in grey concrete bands from bank to bank. It cannot rise and it cannot rest. It begs every passing Garou to break one band, just one. Each broken band floods a few blocks of the South Side’s Penumbra.

u-warden.name: The Concrete Warden
u-warden.html: A square, tireless Weaver spirit that patrols the channel and pours new concrete over every crack. It believes absolutely that it saves lives, and it may be right.

u-kkmouth.name: Where the chains begin
u-kkmouth.html: At the mouth of the channel the bands end and the river spills free into the harbor in a burst of green light. Spirits come here to watch it breathe.

u-polishmoon.name: The Polish Moon
u-polishmoon.sub: The four-faced clock and its Lune court
