u-polishmoon.html: The great clock tower is, in the Umbra, a second moon that never wanes, ringed by Lunes who dance in silver silks. The Moonkeeper holds court on the clock face and enforces every oath sworn beneath it. A Garou who wants to swear something that will hold comes here.

u-reassembled.name: The Reassembled
u-reassembled.sub: The basilica built from another city’s stones
u-reassembled.html: The South Side’s great basilica was raised in 1901 from the salvaged stone of a demolished Chicago building. Its spirit is a patient patchwork giant who remembers being something else and loves being this. It shelters spirits who have lost their homes.

u-bazaar.name: The Mitchell Street Bazaar
u-bazaar.html: Under the shop signs of the old commercial street, small spirits trade favours, fetishes, gossip and Gnosis by the thimbleful. Mouse Garou come here to buy talens. Marta Kaczmarek’s Hearth is just down the street on the Dreaming side, and the Bazaar’s spirits can smell it as warm bread from another world.

u-kosciuszko.name: Kosciuszko’s Watch
u-kosciuszko.sub: The park statue and its sentinel spirit
u-kosciuszko.html: The general’s statue in the park has a spirit that stands guard over the neighbourhood and challenges any Bane that crosses the Ward. It has a soldier’s courtesy and a soldier’s grudges.

u-treaty.name: The Treaty Green
u-treaty.sub: Where the three clans may meet
u-treaty.html: A circle of lawn above the ravines where the Lake Park Truce holds. Any Garou may call a moot here; any who come are safe while they stay on the Green. The Lake Breeze witnesses every word and carries a report of any broken truce to every caern in the city.

u-lighthouse.name: North Point Light
u-lighthouse.html: The old lighthouse burns in the Umbra with a silver flame that lights every moon bridge in the city. When the bridges are open its beam sweeps; when one is broken the beam stutters, and the Lunes come to see why.

u-ravinekids.name: The Ravine Children
u-ravinekids.sub: Wyld spirits of the park ravines
u-ravinekids.html: Small, giggling Wyld spirits of creeks, leaf-litter and rope swings. They obey the paths as a game and break the rule whenever they think nobody is looking.

u-greatwater.name: Greatwater
u-greatwater.html: Not a person but a presence: a vast, cold, patient intelligence under the waves. It speaks in fog, ice and storm. It has never taken a side in the city’s wars, and every Garou Theurge in Milwaukee has tried at least once to change that.

u-usla.name: The Drowned Thief
u-usla.html: When Usla crawled into the lake to die, Greatwater kept him. His spirit lies in the cold dark offshore, chained by his own shame, a broken Garou of the old days who stole two totems’ strength to save a people who were not his. He can tell the truth of the theft. He wants to be asked.

u-alewives.name: The Thousand Alewives
u-alewives.sub: A swarm-spirit of the lake’s die-offs
u-alewives.html: In the 1960s, dead alewives washed up on Milwaukee’s beaches in their millions. Their memory is a shimmering swarm-spirit, silver and mournful, that circles the southern shore and remembers every spill and every poison poured into the lake.

u-avoided.name: The Avoided Water
u-avoided.sub: A place offshore that spirits steer around
u-avoided.html: There is a stretch of open water east of the harbor that every lake-spirit steers around, as though something very large once sat there and might come back. The Garou don’t know why. The fae would call it the Far Guest’s Seat; on this side there is only the gap.

u-wrecks.name: The Wreck-Choir
u-wrecks.html: Schooners, steamers and ore boats lie on the lake floor, and their spirits sing to each other in the dark: a slow choir of bells, fog-horns and timbers. Sailors who hear it in the waking world feel suddenly homesick.

u-icemother.name: Ice-Mother’s Remnant
u-icemother.sub: The glacier that never fully left
u-icemother.html: Far out in the Deep Umbra of the lake lies a blue-white memory of the ice sheet that carved it: Ice-Mother, mostly asleep. In hard winters she stirs, and the Ice Road on the death side freezes in sympathy.

u-breeze.name: The Lake Breeze
u-breeze.sub: The spirit that cools the shore
u-breeze.html: A brisk, cheerful, slightly smug air-spirit, known to every Milwaukeean from the weather report: cooler by the lake. It witnesses the Lake Park Truce and keeps the shore calm. It does not like the Lupine raiders who use its beaches, but it has never once refused them passage.

u-bonfire.name: Bradford Beach bonfires
u-bonfire.html: Small fire-spirits born from a century of summer beach fires, banked for the autumn and dreaming of July. Wake one early and it will burn very bright and very briefly for you.

u-southbluff.name: Grant Park’s wild bluff
u-southbluff.html: Steep wooded ravines down to the lake, the last wild shore in the county. In the Umbra the Eagle clan’s raiders come ashore here after swimming north along the coast, and the Lake Breeze cools their Rage just enough to keep them hidden.

u-rendezvous.name: The rendezvous boat
u-rendezvous.sub: Where the Mouse meet the Union
u-rendezvous.html: Turk’s broken riverboat on the Veterans Park shore has a spirit too: a sad old paddle-steamer that remembers excursions. The Mouse pack’s messenger, Drake, met the Union here during Psychomachia. There is no Mouse pack to deal with any more, but the boat still keeps a lamp lit for him.

u-knot.name: The Knot
u-knot.html: Where three freeways meet, the Weaver has tied an enormous knot of shining lanes. Pattern Spiders keep it tight, and Gridlock Jagglings graze its ramps at rush hour. The Penumbra shows the faint outlines of the streets and houses that were cleared for it. On the death side of the Shroud, the same place is a Nihil.

u-bridgenowhere.name: The Bridge to Nowhere
u-bridgenowhere.html: For years the great lakefront bridge stood finished and unconnected while the city argued over its approaches, and Milwaukee called it the bridge to nowhere. Its spirit still suspects it is unwanted. It is shy, melancholy and enormous, and it will carry anyone who tells it where they are going.

u-parkeast.name: The Park East Spur
u-parkeast.sub: A freeway that dreams of being torn down
u-parkeast.html: A short, unloved elevated spur north of downtown. Its spirit is convinced it will be demolished one day and has made its peace with that. It spends its nights apologising to the neighbourhood beneath it.

u-tolls.name: The Zoo Interchange tollkeepers
u-tolls.html: At the great western interchange, square Weaver spirits demand a token from every spirit crossing between city and suburb. Garou who refuse are re-routed into the Lawn Sea for a very long night.

u-ninthinning.name: The Ninth Inning
u-ninthinning.html: Fifty thousand hopes, every summer, for decades: the stadium’s spirit is a roaring, optimistic giant that wakes for home games and sleeps all winter. Gnosis pours off it on a good night, and Theurges of every clan quietly come to drink.

u-hush.name: The Hush
u-hush.html: Murmur, a Bane of despair, drifts through the old asylum wards like a grey mist. It feeds on every shout and every unanswered plea. The excavation of the poor-farm graves has stirred it up badly.

u-lantern.name: The Healers’ Lantern
u-lantern.html: A gentle spirit carrying a lamp through the wards: the remembered care of every nurse who sat up with a dying stranger. It will help any Garou who comes to heal, and no Garou who comes to fight.

u-embassy.name: The Embassy of Beasts
u-embassy.html: Lion-spirits, bear-spirits, a very old elephant-spirit who chairs the council, and a hundred more, all keeping court behind the zoo walls. They receive Garou as ambassadors and trade news of faraway Umbral lands for news of the lake.

u-greyamb.name: The Grey Ambassador
u-greyamb.html: Wise, sad and patient, the spirit of the captive wolves speaks for every caged pack in the world. Lupus-born Garou find it unbearable and come back anyway.

u-spindle.name: The Departure Spindle
u-spindle.html: A turning tower of light that spins flight paths into the sky. It is the most reliable way out of the city’s Umbra, and the Pattern Spiders keep a manifest of everything that leaves.

u-hive.name: The Southridge Hive
u-hive.html: The big southern mall glows in the Umbra like a honeycomb, full of drone-spirits of want and price-tags. Its Hive-Queen is half Weaver, half something hungrier, and is quietly expanding her territory into the woods.

u-mowers.name: The Mowing Spiders
u-mowers.html: Pale, flat, many-legged Weaver spirits that trim back everything Wyld in the suburbs each week. They are harmless unless you are a weed.

u-marked.name: The Marked Threshold
u-marked.sub: Hrothulf’s house, as the spirits see it
u-marked.html: The book says the Lupine avoid Hrothulf’s suburban house. In the Umbra the reason is plain: an old ancestor-mark of Usla’s band burns over the door. Hrothulf, the vampire, once married into the people Usla fought for and against. The Garou ancestors keep that debt, though no living Garou knows what it is.

u-coyotecaern.name: Caern of the Grinning Stone
u-coyotecaern.sub: The Coyote clan’s caern · limestone quarries
u-coyotecaern.html: A flooded quarry whose cliff-face is cut in the shape of a grin. The caern is small but strong, its Gnosis tasting of dust and lightning. Horatio’s sept of a dozen Red Talon wolves keeps it, and all but two of them have never worn a human face for more than an hour. The totem’s avatar sits on the rim of the quarry laughing. The moon bridge to the Granary broke this autumn, and the caern feels the break like an aching tooth.

u-coyotebawn.name: The Bawn of Echoes
u-coyotebawn.html: Woods and quarry roads that repeat every footstep three times. Intruders hear themselves surrounded long before the Coyote decide to show themselves.

u-oldfalls.name: Old Falls
u-oldfalls.sub: The spirit of the falls at Menomonee Falls
u-oldfalls.html: A small waterfall that gave a town its name. Its spirit is an old friend of the Coyote and keeps their secrets in its roar.

u-grinavatar.name: Coyote’s Grin
u-grinavatar.html: A lean, laughing coyote with one eye blind, the one Usla took. It is the totem’s avatar and the clan’s patron. It is cunning, generous, cruel, and very much wants its eye back.

u-quarrylake.name: The Quarry Lake That Answers
u-quarrylake.html: Throw a stone in and ask a question. The lake answers with a joke. The joke is always true; it just takes a while to understand.

u-eaglecaern.name: Caern of the Bleeding Pine
u-eaglecaern.sub: The Eagle clan’s caern · Root River woods
u-eaglecaern.html: A huge white pine whose sap runs red. It has bled since the night Usla took the Talon. The caern is fierce, small and failing a little each year, and its eight Wendigo guard it with the bitterness of people who know they are losing. This autumn the blight reached its roots: the ward-stones around the pine are defiled, and the sap at its base has started to run black.

u-aerie.name: The Talonless Aerie
u-aerie.html: A ring of tall trees where the clan holds its councils and sings the Grudge, the long, unending list of wrongs done to the Eagle, starting with Usla and ending, for now, with the Kindred of Milwaukee and the Tremere who poisoned the woods. Here too the pack settles business no mortal partner hears about: the Seven Fires casino, held through trusted people, pays for lawyers, land and scholarships, and its board are people Agnes would trust with her life.

u-woundedeagle.name: The Wounded Eagle
u-woundedeagle.html: A white eagle the size of a barn, circling high over the southern woods with one foot clenched and empty. Its cry carries for miles in the Umbra. It is proud, wounded and furious, and it has never forgiven anyone.

u-boerner.name: The Gardeners’ Truce
u-boerner.html: Inside the big county park, the botanical gardens’ cultivated flower-spirits live in a strict, fragrant peace with the wild woods around them. Even the Eagle don’t fight here; they come to sit.

u-gnaw.name: Gnaw
u-gnaw.sub: The Bane that rides the Eagle’s rage
u-gnaw.html: A thin, grinning rage-Bane that clings to the clan’s raiders like a tick and whispers to their Rage. It has grown fat this year on blood that isn’t Garou blood. Parovich is gone, but the feeding trough isn’t empty: the leftovers of Velez’s Sabbat bring the blood now, and in the blighted woods Gnaw finds food of its own. Brother Sparrow can hear it and thinks it is the Eagle speaking.

u-dotfarm.name: Brennan’s farm
u-dotfarm.html: A failing dairy farm where the Brennan family has quietly raised Eagle Kinfolk for four generations. Dot Brennan feeds the clan, hides its wounded and is the only person who can make Agnes Hightree laugh.

u-granary.name: The Granary Caern
u-granary.sub: The Mouse clan’s defiled urban caern
u-granary.html: A caern hidden in the cellars of the old produce warehouses. It used to smell of grain, onions and candle-wax and fed on the city’s hunger the way a field feeds on rain. Now it smells of rotten grain and copper. Jesselin and McKenzie defiled its heart with a blood rite, and Banes have bred in the lower cellars: grey, small, countless, gnawing sacks and spirits alike. The caern is dying. Grandmother Mouse still sleeps in its heart but no longer answers. Mercer keeps the last candles lit.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The caern can still be saved: the cleansing rite needs Garou of three clans in one cellar. Mercer doesn’t know it. Horatio suspects.

u-grandmouse.name: Grandmother Mouse
u-grandmouse.html: A tiny, ancient, silver-furred mouse wearing a thimble for a hat. She was the most dangerous spirit in the Warrens because she had survived everything. She survived this too, barely. She lies curled in her thimble, weak and silent, her fur gone dull.

u-commission.name: Commission Row kin
u-commission.sub: The Wójcik family and the market workers
u-commission.html: Mouse Kinfolk families have worked the produce trade for generations: truckers, stall-holders, night watchmen. They know the clan without quite knowing what it is, and they keep its doors.

u-ericasroom.name: Erica’s empty place
u-ericasroom.sub: Where Merik’s wife used to sleep · now a memorial room
u-ericasroom.html: A small cellar room in the Warrens kept exactly as Erica left it. She was a Gangrel the Mouse accepted as packmate, the rarest thing a vampire can earn. Mira Kessler knew why Erica stopped coming, but Mira is dead and the secret died with her. Mercer has put candles here for all of them: Erica, Rosa, Teodor, Mira, and two unlit ones for Benny and Drake. Gunther, Erica’s old friend, sometimes sits here with him until dawn.

u-hedgelords.name: The Hedgerow Lords
u-hedgelords.sub: Estate spirits of the North Shore
u-hedgelords.html: Proud, clipped spirits of old estates and their boundary hedges. They take trespass very seriously and everything else not at all. They have been known to hire Banes as watchmen.

u-doctorsravine.name: Doctors Park ravine
u-doctorsravine.sub: An old Wyld fold on the north shore
u-doctorsravine.html: A steep, wild ravine to the lake where the Hedgerow Lords’ writ does not run. Mouse Garou go to ground here when the city is too much.

u-mousecave.name: The cave on Route 43
u-mousecave.html: In the Umbra the little cave is a hall of bones with a low door. The Justicar’s remains lay at the back. A spirit of the cave, the Bone-Count, remembers every body ever brought in. Since Psychomachia it has been asking who will come to collect the Justicar’s.

u-thiensville.name: The mill-dam spirit
u-thiensville.html: An old mill-dam spirit, slow and courteous, that keeps the northern river’s memory and trades it for news of the city.

u-lapham.name: Lapham’s Watcher
u-lapham.sub: The weather-spirit on the high hill
u-lapham.html: On the high hill at Delafield, where the state’s first weather observations were made, a careful spirit watches the sky and writes down everything it sees. It is the best forecaster in the Umbra, and it will warn the clans of storms if asked politely.

u-kettles.name: The Kettles
u-kettles.html: Round glacial ponds that in the Umbra are eyes of the old ice, watching the sky. Garou Theurges come to read them.

u-bog.name: The Bog of First Waters
u-bog.html: Mist and peat-light, and things too old to have shapes. Visiting is safe. Staying is not.

u-unnamed.name: The Unnamed
u-unnamed.sub: Something at the bottom of the bog
u-unnamed.html: A Wyld presence older than the bog. It does not speak; it changes those who listen. Every clan has a story about the Garou who went down to ask it something and came back different.

u-holyhill.name: The sealed caern
u-holyhill.sub: The summit of the Hill of Two Prayers
u-holyhill.html: A great caern, sealed with a rite nobody living remembers. Its moon bridges are cold. In the Umbra the hill wears a crown of stars and a basilica of light, and pilgrims of two faiths climb it side by side.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The seal was set by Usla’s band before their last battle. The Drowned Thief remembers the rite. An open caern could give Mercer a new home, or become the place where three clans finally make one sept.

u-edge.name: The Hunting Edge crossroads
u-edge.html: Claw-scored road and the ghosts of a hundred ambushes. Decker’s motel is a block south. The Anubi and the Lupine both leave signs here for the other to read.

u-ancestors.name: The Ancestor Hollows
u-ancestors.sub: Forest Home, as the Garou see it
u-ancestors.html: The ancestor-spirits of three clans’ bloodlines gather among the old graves: grandmothers, great-uncles, a lupus elder who died in the 1918 snow. They are not wraiths. They are the remembered strength of family. Kinfolk of all three clans lie here together.

u-domes.name: The Kept Wild
u-domes.html: The jungle dome’s spirits are restless and want to go out into the Wisconsin winter. The desert dome’s spirits think they are mad. The show garden changes sides depending on the season.

u-northdam.name: The North Avenue Dam
u-northdam.html: A sullen, patient river-spirit pooled behind the old dam, remembering every word spoken over its water. It believes the dam will come down one day. It’s right, though nobody in 1991 would bet on it.

u-estabrook.name: Estabrook Falls
u-estabrook.html: A short run of rapids where the river is loud and free. Garou who want to talk without being overheard by the Dammed Reach come here, below its reach.

u-soldiers.name: The Battle-Echo
u-soldiers.sub: The Soldiers Home, as war-spirits see it
u-soldiers.html: Spirits of old battles gather around the veterans’ cemetery like crows on a fence. Ahroun of every clan come to sit with them before a fight.

u-crucible.name: The Crucible’s hunger
u-crucible.html: The Kindred’s central hunting ground shows in the Umbra as a dim, sticky patch where small Banes collect like flies. Garou who know what they are looking at can tell how many vampires fed there last night.

g-pangaea.name: The path to Pangaea
g-pangaea.html: At the bottom of the bog a path opens into the Realm of Pangaea, the world as it was before people. Those who come back describe mammoth-spirits, and the smell of the first rain.

g-cyber.name: The Data-Sky
g-cyber.sub: Gate to the Weaver’s Cyber Realm
g-cyber.html: From the top of the Spire, a thread leads up into the Cyber Realm: a city of pure pattern, lit by phosphor and paperwork. The Pattern Spiders guard it jealously.

g-malfeas.name: The Rendering Pit
g-malfeas.html: Deep in the valley a pit of boiling tallow opens downward toward the Wyrm’s own realm. Tallow guards it. Parovich does not know it exists. He would be very interested.

g-aether.name: The Lunar Stair
g-aether.html: The Moonkeeper can open a silver stair from the clock face to the Aetherial Realm, where the stars live. She does it once a year, for a price nobody has yet agreed to pay.

g-battle.name: The War-Field gate
g-battle.html: At the heart of the veterans’ cemetery a road leads into the Battleground, the realm of endless war. Ahroun go there to train, and some do not come back.

g-legend.name: The Legendary Way
g-legend.html: Behind the sealed caern a dim road leads to the Legendary Realm, where every story ever told about the Garou is true. Reopening the caern would light it.

g-fork.name: Where the Silver Path forks
g-fork.html: Lunes whisper that far out over Greatwater the moon’s road splits in two, and that one branch leads toward Arcadia. No local Garou has found the fork. The fae, on their own side of things, would say the Dreaming is not the Umbra, and they would be right.

u-wardstone.name: The defiled ward-stone
u-wardstone.sub: A guardian stone turned against the forest
u-wardstone.html: A boulder carved with Wendigo signs, which held the forest’s Gauntlet for a hundred years, split in two, the crack filled with caked blood. The House Goratrix rite turned the ward inside out: the stone no longer holds Banes back but calls them, and the Gauntlet around it has worn to a rag. Brother Sparrow has tried to cleanse it twice and twice retreated with burns.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: Burned into the stone’s underside are sigils Mercer would recognise: the same as in the Granary’s defiled heart. This is Jesselin’s hand; McKenzie only paid in blood.

u-banenest.name: The Bane nest
u-banenest.sub: A rotting hollow where they breed
u-banenest.html: A hollow where a spring used to rise, now choked with oily fog. In the Penumbra the trunks are covered with blisters, and Banes hatch from the blisters: small biting things like flayed ferrets, and larger things Coal-Eye won’t talk about. The Eagle burn the nest out every week. Every week it grows back.

u-blackcreek.name: The poisoned creek
u-blackcreek.sub: Water carrying the blight toward people
u-blackcreek.html: A creek running out of the blighted wood toward the Franklin farms. Its spirit is sick and raving, and in the Umbra its water is the colour of rust. Mortals see only dead fish and sick cattle; Dot Brennan sees more.

gp-grand.name: The Well Hall
gp-grand.html: The huge round chamber of an old storm-water well, turned into an assembly hall. Here Mother Agatha receives petitioners and the Nosferatu decide what the city knows.

gp-archive.name: The rumour archive
gp-archive.html: The newspaper’s old pneumatic-post vault: rows of drawers with a card on every resident of the city, by night and by day. Cricket keeps the file and listens to the telephone lines.

gp-ratking.name: The Rat King
gp-ratking.html: A thousand rats fed on Nosferatu blood, their tails knotted into a single creature. The Rat King guards the western approaches to the Warrens and squeaks to Agatha about everyone who comes.

gp-market.name: The Rat Market
gp-market.html: Stalls made of crates, lanterns on hooks, hooded traders. Information, papers, weapons, blood. The only place underground where the Nosferatu are glad to see strangers.

gp-parovich.name: Parovich’s abandoned rooms
gp-parovich.html: The former Primogen’s den under his mansion. The Council searched and sealed it: letters to Velez, a map of the tunnels, an empty coffin. The seals are intact. The bricks of the old passage have been broken out from inside.

notes.title: Storyteller
notes.html: The vozhd came here. The Parovich inside it wanted to see his home.

gp-pocketdoor.name: The harbour lock
gp-pocketdoor.sub: Where the way under the lake begins
gp-pocketdoor.html: An old lock at the edge of the harbour. From here a passage slopes down under the lake to the Michigan Pocket. The grate is held by a Nosferatu padlock and a sluagh seal. Brother Dust keeps watch.

gp-akawa.name: The cell under MECCA
gp-akawa.html: A concrete boiler room turned into a cell in the Council’s steam tunnels. Akawa sits here, under a blood bond and the guard of Gracis’s ghouls. The Blood Brothers don’t know where he is. The Nosferatu do.

gp-pocketdoor2.name: The Undersea Door
gp-pocketdoor2.sub: The Pocket’s entrance from the Warrens’ side
gp-pocketdoor2.html: A door from an old bank vault set into the cave wall. On this side hangs a sign in Gaelic: “Closed until forgiven.”

gp-gas.name: The Robinson gas station
gp-gas.html: A gas station with a faded logo and working neon. The pumps still give fuel nobody ever delivered. Ivory took it when the building was condemned. Jamie Robinson came here once, and left without a word.

gp-diner.name: The diner
gp-diner.html: A chrome dining car with a DINER sign. The sluagh gather here to whisper. There is always a pie in the fridge that nobody baked.

gp-gazebo.name: The gazebo
gp-gazebo.html: An octagonal bandstand where an orchestra played in the 1920s. Some nights there is music in it.

gp-houses.name: The street of forgotten houses
gp-houses.html: Frame houses from the north side, torn down for the freeway. The sluagh carried them off with their wallpaper, the photographs on the walls and the smell of supper. The doors aren’t locked.

gp-pens.name: The pens
gp-pens.html: Wooden pens from the valley’s old stockyards. Empty. The sluagh brought them so the city wouldn’t forget what was killed in the valley.

gp-boxcar.name: The boxcar
gp-boxcar.html: A rusted boxcar without wheels. Inside is a storeroom of signs, shop fronts, lamps and door handles: the small things that don’t fit in buildings.

gp-truss.name: The bridge truss
gp-truss.sub: A span of a demolished railroad bridge
gp-truss.html: A steel truss lies on the rocks over a black crack. They say that if you cross it you come out somewhere other than where you went in.

gp-angels.name: The angels
gp-angels.html: Stone angels from moved and demolished cemeteries stand along the road, facing the way out. The Nosferatu set them up; that was their share of the work.

gp-lion.name: The stone lion and the memorials
gp-lion.html: A lion from the façade of a demolished bank, a nameless obelisk, an abstract sculpture the city council declared “ugly”. The Pocket keeps even what nobody liked.

gp-spire.name: The spire
gp-spire.sub: The steeple of a demolished church
gp-spire.html: A white wooden steeple lying on a heap of brick. The bell inside sometimes rings by itself, at the death of another building above.

gp-gallery.name: The Gallery of Two Peoples
gp-gallery.sub: The shared place of the sluagh and the Nosferatu
gp-gallery.html: A cave wall covered with drawings, names and dates: for generations the Nosferatu and the sluagh recorded here which building was saved and by whom. The last Nosferatu entry is from 1990. After it there is only Ivory’s handwriting.

gp-ivory.name: Ivory’s lookout
gp-ivory.sub: Where she watches over the Pocket
gp-ivory.html: A wooden fire tower from a hill outside town. Ivory sits at the top in her school uniform doing homework while the stolen city sleeps below her.

gp-wide.name: The gate of Warehouse No. 7
gp-wide.sub: The mouth of Dragos’s wide tunnel
gp-wide.html: The back wall of the warehouse hides a gentle ramp a truck wide. The Camarilla has put a grate and a couple of ghouls here. The grate has been bent from inside twice already.

gp-shaft-ji.name: The Jones Island shaft
gp-shaft-ji.html: A vertical shaft of the tunnel under construction, by the treatment plant. A single watchman is on duty at night; he has twice been found asleep at the bottom.

gp-shaft-n.name: The North Avenue shaft
gp-shaft-n.html: The northern shaft of the Deep Tunnel. Gunther goes down here when he wants to cross the city unseen.

gp-shaft-v.name: The valley shaft
gp-shaft-v.html: An abandoned construction shaft in the middle of the valley. The workers left after a night shift didn’t come back up.

gp-miller.name: The Miller caves
gp-miller.html: Cold cellars in the hillside. Tours by day; by night, a neutral waystation of the Nosferatu and the Gangrel.

gp-chestnut.name: The Chestnut Street cellars
gp-chestnut.html: Vaulted cellars where ice for the lager was stored. From here you can reach the Spine without going up to the street.

gp-bridge.name: The door under the bridge
gp-bridge.html: The service door under the Wisconsin Avenue bridge, from the inside: a short brick passage straight into the Spine. Nobody forces it. That is the whole agreement.

gp-usla.name: Usla’s burial
gp-usla.sub: Under St. Joan of Arc Chapel
gp-usla.html: A narrow crack in the dolomite directly under the chapel. Here Usla hid the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote in his own hand and eye. The stone is warm to the touch. No spell works. Haberman would give a year of his unlife to get in here.

gp-ossuary.name: The bone workshop
gp-ossuary.html: A tannery basement where Dragos sculpted his creatures. Tables of fused bone, walls laced with sinew, jars of eyes on the shelves. Castor lives here and carries on his master’s work.

gp-hounds.name: Dragos’s hounds
gp-hounds.html: Six, or by now five, things the size of calves, with human hands for forepaws. They hunt as a pack in the valley sewers and can smell vampire blood.

gp-choir.name: The Choir
gp-choir.html: Prisoners from the viaduct, sewn into one crawling body with a dozen mouths. The Choir sings the hymns its parts remember and weeps when it is fed.

gp-gills.name: The Gills
gp-gills.sub: Fish-men from the sewers by the fish plant
gp-gills.html: What Dragos made out of fish and people on the plant’s conveyor. A few survived and went down into the harbour sewers. Cold, slippery, and sometimes they climb out onto the piers.

gp-wall.name: The living wall
gp-wall.html: A partition of flesh grown across the tunnel to slow pursuit. It still breathes and grabs at anything that comes too close.

gp-stalker.name: The Faceless
gp-stalker.sub: A loner in the southern galleries
gp-stalker.html: A tall thing without a face that repeats the voices it hears. It lures hunters and the homeless with the voices of their families.

gp-shovel.name: The shovelhead dugout
gp-shovel.html: A side gallery where three of Velez’s shovelheads, dug out of their graves too late to fight, have learned to live like animals. Noemí visits them with blood once a week and calls them “the reserves”.

gp-vozd.name: The vozhd
gp-vozd.html: A colossal thing of dozens of fused bodies fills the drift from wall to wall. It sleeps until disturbed. One of the faces in its flank is Parovich. He never sleeps.

gp-drake.name: The spiral den
gp-drake.html: A culvert scored with clawed spirals. Drake sleeps in a concrete pipe and sometimes goes up into the Penumbra.

gp-cistern.name: The Black Water cistern
gp-cistern.html: A flooded brick hall with a single dry island in the middle. Noemí and her pack sleep on it in sleeping bags. Hieronymus performs the Vaulderie here.

gp-maxcache.name: Maximus’s cache
gp-maxcache.sub: In a sewer under Bay View
gp-maxcache.html: A niche behind a sewer grate: boxes of totem blanks, blood in ampoules, a list of buyers. Maximus comes back here once a week.

t-lupine.name: Lupine lands
t-lupine.html: Everything past the Anubi patrol line belongs to the Werewolves. Roads, rail and the suburbs beyond are hunting ground; few Kindred cross them alive, and none do it by choice. Even Shorewood, the North Shore and their lakefront parks fall outside any Kindred patrol.

t-anubi.name: The Outlands (Anubi patrol zone)
t-anubi.html: The no-man’s-land of suburbs between the city and the wilds. Mark Decker’s Anubi patrol its outer edge every night, ambushing Lupine raiders before they reach the Barrens. The border drawn here is their outermost patrol route; Good Hope Road marks its northern limit.
t-anubi.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; Geography p. 18; Kindred p. 35

t-bb.name: Blood Brothers territory
t-bb.html: The largest slice of the Barrens, from West-Downtown out to the Zoo Freeway. Most Anarch rumbles happen here, since downtown is too well watched by the Elders. Akawa’s Blood Brothers used to leave quiet travellers alone, but since their leader was captured the gang is in turmoil, and nobody can vouch for its streets.
t-bb.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; West-Downtown p. 22

t-union.name: Union turf: East Downtown & the lakeshore
t-union.html: Turk’s Union clings to the narrow lakeside strip east of the Milwaukee River, from the UWM end of the East Side down through the Lower East Side and the I-794 corridor into Bay View. The Union leaves Elders alone but mauls Neonates who wander in alone. Since Merik used them as his pawns, the gang is bleeding members and losing ground to the Blood Brothers.
t-union.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; East Downtown p. 26

t-elders-dt.name: Elder control: downtown core
t-elders-dt.html: The glass-and-steel heart of Kindred Milwaukee, spanning the river around MECCA, the Hyatt and City Hall. The Council meets here, the oldest havens are here, and heavy police patrols keep the street-level riff-raff away. Anarchs fight elsewhere; the Elders watch from the penthouses.
t-elders-dt.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; pp. 22–24

t-elders-air.name: Elder control: General Mitchell Field
t-elders-air.html: With every road and rail line running through Lupine country, the airport is the city’s real front door. The Council holds it tightly. Gracis’s spies log every arrival; Parovich’s orphaned network passed to the Warrens after his exposure, and nobody knows who it reports to now.
t-elders-air.src: Milwaukee by Night, War Map p. 21; Geography p. 18

t-null.name: The Marquette null zone
t-null.html: A “magic-dead” zone covering Marquette’s campus: north past Mount Sinai Medical Center, west to the old Children’s Hospital, south almost to the Menomonee. Thaumaturgy fails here and Paths risk aggravated backlash, while Auspex and Protean grow stronger. The cause lies under St. Joan of Arc Chapel: Usla’s buried totems.
t-null.src: Milwaukee by Night, History p. 13; Geography p. 20; Tremere p. 50

t-crucible.name: The Crucible
t-crucible.html: Milwaukee’s central hunting grounds, a West-Downtown knot of bars and dance clubs. No faction has tried to claim it yet. Its exact blocks are not given in the book; this outline places it on the west bank just south of the MECCA complex.
t-crucible.src: Milwaukee by Night, Things to Do, pp. 23–24

t-coyote.name: Range of the Coyote pack
t-coyote.html: The principal Lupine pack, just under a dozen strong, and every one a Red Talon, a lupus wolf. It is led by the coolly rational wolf the Kindred call Horatio Sims. Horatio wants one thing: the Kindred off balance long enough for him to hold Marquette and dig up the totems. This autumn his wolves are also helping the Eagle burn Banes out of the southern woods. The book does not map pack ranges; the western and northwestern Outlands are assigned here.
t-coyote.src: Milwaukee by Night, Lupine p. 69; placement is Storyteller discretion

t-eagle.name: Range of the Eagle pack
t-eagle.html: About eight Garou, almost all Wendigo, who hate the Kindred so much that they raid the city roughly once a week regardless of odds. They blame the Coyote for the theft of their totem’s Talon. The pack keeps human ties among the city’s Native Americans and secretly owns the Seven Fires casino. This autumn the Goratrix Tremere poisoned their woods with Banes, and the raids have mostly stopped. Placed along the southern approaches, astride I-94 and the Chicago corridor.
t-eagle.src: Milwaukee by Night, Lupine p. 70; placement is Storyteller discretion

t-mouse.name: Range of the Mouse pack
t-mouse.html: Once fifteen Garou, mostly Glass Walkers, who hated Vampires even by Lupine standards. They lived in the city in human form, and Merik’s Gangrel wife ran with them. In Psychomachia they ambushed the Mask on Route 43 north. Since then the Sabbat and the House Goratrix Tremere have almost wiped out and corrupted the pack; of the old Mouse only Mercer remains. The range is the northern woods and the North Shore lakefront.
t-mouse.src: Milwaukee by Night, Lupine p. 70; A Midnight Moon

t-dz-cudahy.name: Danger: the Cudahy warehouse yards
t-dz-cudahy.html: Where Dragos’s spawn came up into the city. A Camarilla gate and two ghouls now guard the wide ramp behind Warehouse No. 7, and the gate has twice been bent from below. Stray dogs won’t enter the yards. Night-shift workers have stopped taking the shortcut along the tracks.

t-dz-valley.name: Danger: Tannery Row
t-dz-valley.html: The old tanneries and packing houses above the flesh tunnels. At night things come up through the drains to hunt: Dragos’s hounds, the Choir’s outflung limbs. Blood Brothers cross the valley in pairs now, and never on foot after 3 a.m.

t-dz-harbor.name: Danger: the fish-plant cordon
t-dz-harbor.html: Police tape, a security trailer and the smell of burnt ammonia. Under the piers live the Gills: things Dragos made of fish and men on the plant’s conveyors. They climb out onto the docks on foggy nights.

t-dz-blight.name: Danger: the blighted Root River woods
t-dz-blight.html: The forest the Goratrix Tremere poisoned to keep the Garou busy. Banes pour out of the defiled groves, the Eagle pack fights them every night, and anyone else who wanders in is either a target or a meal.

r-wolf.name: The Country of the Wolf’s Eye

uz-thicket.name: The Glass Thicket
uz-thicket.sub: Downtown, as the Weaver sees it
uz-thicket.html: Downtown’s Umbral reflection is a forest of crystal: towers grown from spun glass, skywalks thick with web, and bank vaults ringing like bells. Pattern Spiders the size of buses walk the parapets, reinforcing the Gauntlet strand by strand. The few Wyld spirits left live in the cracks and pay rent to clerks. Kindred havens show here as cold, rotten spots that the spiders refuse to touch.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything must be counted. A spirit that cannot give its number is unmade and filed. Garou who step sideways here must name themselves aloud before the Pattern Spiders let them move.

uz-claw.name: The Clawed Sky
uz-claw.sub: Over Marquette and the buried relics
uz-claw.html: The book’s “magic-dead” zone is, in the Umbra, a permanent storm. Two halves of two totems, the Talon of the Eagle and the Eye of the Coyote, lie under St. Joan of Arc Chapel. Each yearns for its owner so hard that the sky above Marquette is torn open in long red scratches. A great eye watches from the clouds on one side and a talon rakes them on the other. The Gauntlet slams shut and swings open like a door in wind.

facts.v: 2–9, flickering
Totemic storm

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything happens twice. Every Gift, rite and spirit summoned here arrives doubled: one answer from the Eagle’s side and one from the Coyote’s. The two answers never agree.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: Horatio’s pack and the Eagle both have a Theurge camped at the storm’s edge. Neither has noticed that Dr. Mortius has strung wards along the zone’s north side, and those wards are starting to hum.

uz-gambrinus.name: Gambrinus Hill
uz-gambrinus.html: Beer has been brewed on this hill since the 1840s, and its spirit has grown into a crowned old king of copper, foam and civic pride who calls himself Gambrinus. His halls are a smoky Bavarian banquet that never ends. He is ailing: the brewery is losing money, and in the Umbra the vats are running low.

facts.v: Genius loci

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Hospitality must be accepted. Refuse an offered drink and you have declared a feud; accept it and you may not raise a claw until you leave the hill.

uz-copper.name: The Copper Queen’s Valley
uz-copper.html: The biggest brewery left in town has a spirit to match: a vast, bright Copper Queen in a crown of hop-vines, healthy, rich and expanding. She and Gambrinus are old rivals and occasional lovers. Her court is the busiest in the Penumbra: a beer hall where spirits of every allegiance drink side by side because no one dares break her peace.

facts.v: Genius loci

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Every guest pays in a story. The Queen collects them in barrels, and a story told here becomes common knowledge in every tavern spirit in the city by morning.

uz-dryvats.name: The Dry Vats
uz-dryvats.sub: The closed brewery on the river bluff
uz-dryvats.html: The big brewery on the bluff closed in 1982, and its spirit is dying slowly. The Widow of the Vats walks empty fermenting rooms, still polishing kettles nobody will fill. Weaver salvage-spirits are already measuring the walls for offices.

facts.v: Fading genius

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing new may be started. Gifts of creation and new pacts fail here; only endings, inventories and farewells hold.

uz-ironhorse.name: The Iron Horse Run
uz-ironhorse.html: Next door to the Copper Queen, the motorcycle works breeds chrome Jagglings that run in howling packs. Their lord is the Iron Horse: half engine, half stallion, loud enough to crack the Gauntlet. The Blood Brothers ride its children without knowing it. The spirits have decided that Akawa, who rides in wolf shape, is a strange kind of Garou.

facts.v: Weaver–Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Speed is truth. Whoever arrives first is believed; whoever is passed on the road must concede the argument.

uz-rendering.name: The Rendering
uz-rendering.sub: The Menomonee Valley tanneries and packing houses
uz-rendering.html: A century of stockyards, tanneries and rendering vats has left a spirit-landscape of boiling pits, hide-curtains and rivers of tallow. The ghosts of slaughtered beasts run in terrified herds through the smoke. The Garou should hate it, and do, but nobody has ever been strong enough to cleanse it.

facts.v: Wyrm

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything is reduced. Spirits that linger here are boiled down into simpler and hungrier things, and wounds taken in the valley don’t heal until you leave it.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The stockyard herd-spirits have started stampeding out of the valley at dusk. Something new is driving them, and it smells of the Sabbat.

uz-works.name: The Transmuting Works
uz-works.sub: Jones Island and the sewage-to-fertiliser plant
uz-works.html: The great plant on Jones Island turns the city’s waste into fertiliser, and its Umbral reflection is a cathedral of alchemy where Wyrm-filth goes in and Wyld-green comes out. Grandmother Compost presides, ancient and patient. Wyrm, Weaver and Wyld all claim the Works, and none of them is wrong.

facts.v: Contested

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything given becomes useful. Leave a thing here and the Works will turn it into something else. You don’t choose what.

uz-chained.name: The Chained River
uz-chained.html: In the 1960s the Kinnickinnic was poured into a concrete trough to control its floods. In the Umbra the river spirit lies bound in grey bands, still alive and thrashing. The Concrete Warden patrols the banks and reinforces the chains each night. Freeing the river would flood the South Side’s Penumbra with Wyld water, and some of the spirits who live here like their dry cellars.

facts.v: Weaver over Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing may stop moving. Stand still in the channel and the current, or the Concrete Warden, carries you to the lake.

uz-polishmoon.name: The Ward of the Polish Moon
uz-polishmoon.sub: The South Side under the great clock
uz-polishmoon.html: The four-faced Allen-Bradley clock rises over the South Side, and the neighbourhood calls it the Polish Moon. Lunes love it: a second moon that never wanes. They have built a silver court around it, and moon-folk dance there whether Luna is full or dark. The Mouse pack’s Galliards come here to learn the old songs, and Garou of any clan can swear oaths under it that the Lunes will enforce.

facts.v: Lunar

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Under the Polish Moon the hour is whatever the clock says, and a promise made beneath its face binds until it strikes midnight. After that it binds forever.

uz-accord.name: Olmsted’s Accord
uz-accord.html: A landscape architect laid out these ravines and lawns as a city’s idea of nature, and the spirits took the design seriously. Wyld and Weaver live here by agreement. That agreement made the Accord the one place where the three feuding clans can meet without killing each other, under the Lake Park Truce.

facts.v: Balance

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Paths must be kept. Spirits that leave the designed paths lose their names until dawn, and blood spilled on the Treaty Green is carried by the Lake Breeze to every caern in the city.

notes.title: This autumn
notes.html: The Truce was last invoked in 1983. Horatio wants to call a moot here before the first snow, not for peace this time but for war on the Banes in the poisoned forest. The Eagle have not said whether they will come. From the Mouse, only Mercer can.

uz-lake.name: Greatwater
uz-lake.html: The Umbral lake is a living inland sea, deep blue and lit from below by currents of spirit-light. Wreck-spirits, fish swarms, ice-memories and storms all live in it. Greatwater, the lake’s own vast spirit, is neither friendly nor hostile. It is simply bigger than every quarrel on the shore. Usla went into the lake to die, and Greatwater has kept him.

facts.v: Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: The lake keeps what it takes. What drowns or is thrown into Greatwater belongs to it, and getting anything back requires a gift of equal weight.

uz-breeze.name: The Lake Breeze Strand
uz-breeze.html: A long ribbon of wind, beach and bluff, ruled by the Lake Breeze, the spirit every Milwaukeean knows from the weather report. The book’s Lupines swim the lake and come ashore here to reach the Union. In the Umbra, this is the road they take.

facts.v: Air

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: It is always cooler by the lake. Rage gathers slowly here and frenzy is hard to reach, which is why Lupine raiders use the shore to approach unseen and why they must fight elsewhere.

uz-stitch.name: The Stitchwork
uz-stitch.html: The freeways are the Weaver’s sutures, pulling the city’s spirit-flesh tight along their lines. Where they were cut through neighbourhoods, the Penumbra still shows the outlines of streets that were erased, like scar tissue under the stitches. Gridlock Jagglings graze on the slowdowns.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Keep to your lane. A spirit that crosses the Stitchwork anywhere but at a ramp is thrown back where it came from, and the spiders remember who tried.

uz-hush.name: The Hush
uz-hush.html: Asylums, poor farms and hospitals, a century of them, on one stretch of county land. The Umbra here is soft, grey and quiet, haunted by Murmur, a Bane of despair, and tended by the Healers’ Lantern, a gentle spirit that walks the wards. On the death side of the Shroud, the poor-farm graves are being opened. The spirits feel it as an earthquake.

facts.v: Wyrm & healing

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: No one may raise their voice. Shouted words become Banes of despair. Whispered ones are heard by the healing spirits and sometimes answered.

uz-zoo.name: The Embassy of Beasts
uz-zoo.html: Animal-spirits from every continent are kept here, homesick and dignified. They treat the zoo as a court in exile, receive Garou as visiting diplomats, and trade news of distant Umbral lands for news of the lake. The zoo’s wolves have a spirit of their own, the Grey Ambassador, who speaks for every captive pack.

facts.v: Gaia

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Captivity is honoured as truce. No hunting inside the walls, and any creature here may ask any other for news of its homeland.

uz-spindle.name: The Departure Spindle
uz-spindle.html: A great Weaver spindle spins flight paths into the sky: shining threads to Chicago and everywhere beyond. It is the most reliable way out of the city’s Umbra and the most watched. The Pattern Spiders keep a manifest of every spirit that departs.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything must leave. Spirits can only stay at the airport by holding a ticket for somewhere else; Garou who linger feel an overwhelming urge to go.

uz-lawn.name: The Lawn Sea
uz-lawn.html: Mile after mile of neat, quiet, spirit-poor suburb: hedge-spirits trimmed into shape, lawn-spirits mown flat, malls glowing like hives. This is where Decker’s Anubi ride and where the Lupine raiders cross. The Weaver keeps it tidy. Underneath, the old prairie is still waiting.

facts.v: Weaver

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing may grow above the fence line. Wyld spirits in the suburbs are trimmed back each week, and a Garou who loses her temper on a lawn draws every Mowing Spider in the township.

uz-lawn.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.

uz-coyote.name: Coyote Country
uz-coyote.sub: The quarries and the north-western woods
uz-coyote.html: Limestone quarries, flooded pits and second-growth woods west and north-west of the city, held by Horatio Sims’s Clan of the Coyote. Every one of them is a Red Talon, a wolf born, and to them the human city is a festering wound on Gaia’s body; they go near its lights only when they must. The Penumbra here is ochre and dusty, full of echoes. Coyote’s Grin, the totem’s avatar, can be glimpsed on any ridge, laughing at something nobody else heard.

facts.v: Garou (Coyote · Red Talons)

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Every bargain hides a trick, and the truth may only be spoken as a joke. Spirits here answer a straight question with a riddle, and the Coyote expect you to laugh.

uz-coyote.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.

uz-eagle.name: Eagle Height
uz-eagle.sub: The Root River woods and the southern approaches
uz-eagle.html: Tall pines, river bottoms and farm country south and south-west of the city, held by the Clan of the Eagle. They are fewer than the Coyote, angrier, and they raid the city every week. The sky is white and enormous here, and the Wounded Eagle circles overhead missing one talon, crying for it.

facts.v: Garou (Eagle · Wendigo)

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Nothing is forgiven. Every debt is remembered, and spirits here will repeat to you every wrong you have ever done to an Eagle.

uz-eagle.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.

uz-warrens.name: The Mouse Warrens
uz-warrens.sub: Commission Row, the Third Ward cellars
uz-warrens.html: Beneath the Glass Thicket’s southern edge, under the old produce warehouses of Commission Row, the Clan of the Mouse kept its urban caern. The Umbra here is a maze of grain-sacks, crates and tunnels lit by candle-stubs, and most of the candles have gone out. During the failed Sabbat invasion the House Goratrix Tremere Jesselin and Maximus McKenzie hunted the pack down with the Sabbat: Rosa, Little Teodor and Mira Kessler were killed, Benny and Drake were broken and given to the Wyrm. Of the Mouse’s Glass Walkers only Mercer survives. Erica, Merik’s Gangrel wife, used to run here; hers is no longer the only empty room.

facts.v: Garou (Mouse), failing

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: The small may pass and the large must ask. Any spirit or Garou in a smaller shape used to move freely, and anything bigger than a dog needed a Mouse to vouch for it. Only one Mouse is left to vouch now, and the Banes in the cellars take advantage: they get in because they are small.

uz-hedgerow.name: The Hedgerow Lands
uz-hedgerow.sub: The North Shore and the northern woods
uz-hedgerow.html: The wealthy North Shore and the river ravines beyond it: estates guarded by proud Hedgerow Lords, ravines full of old Wyld, and the north road where the Mouse pack ambushed the Mask on Merik’s orders. The Mouse range here when they leave the city.

facts.v: Weaver & old Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Trespass is the only sin. Crossing a property line without leave is a crime the spirits punish; everything else is forgivable.

uz-hedgerow.src: Improvised for this chronicle. The outline follows the waking map’s range for this territory.

uz-moraine.name: The Moraine
uz-moraine.sub: The Kettle Moraine country, far west
uz-moraine.html: Glacial hills, kettle ponds and kames left by the last ice sheet. In the Umbra the ice has not entirely left: blue-white spirits move under the hills and the ponds look back. Lapham’s Watcher keeps the weather here.

facts.v: Deep Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: The old ice remembers. Weaver things fail here: watches stop, engines stall, and fetishes made in factories go quiet.

uz-bog.name: The Bog of First Waters
uz-bog.sub: The great bog, north of the city
uz-bog.html: An old bog that the Weaver never got its threads into. The Gauntlet is almost nothing here. The Penumbra is mist and peat-light, with things too old to have shapes, and somewhere in the middle there is a path to Pangaea.

facts.v: Deep Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Names dissolve. Stay longer than a night and you forget your own; spirits here have none and want none.

uz-holyhill.name: The Hill of Two Prayers
uz-holyhill.html: The highest ground for miles carries a basilica on its summit and, in the Umbra, a great caern that has been sealed since before any living Garou was born. Christian pilgrims and Gaian spirits both pray here and, unusually, neither minds. Whoever reopens the caern could found a true sept for Milwaukee. The three clans would have to agree on who that is.

facts.v: Sealed caern

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Climb only on foot. No shapeshifting, no step sideways and no flight carries you up the hill; it must be walked.

uz-edge.name: The Hunting Edge
uz-edge.html: The northern boundary of Kindred territory is a raw wound in the Penumbra: claw-scored asphalt, the ghosts of ambushes, and country-club woods full of eyes. Spirits of battle gather here like crows. Decker’s Anubi patrol it every night.

facts.v: War

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: No truce after sunset. Any pact made on Good Hope Road ends when the sun goes down. The Anubi and the Garou both know it, and both use it.

uz-ancestors.name: The Ancestor Hollows
uz-ancestors.sub: Forest Home and the old cemeteries
uz-ancestors.html: Garou ancestor-spirits gather where the city keeps its dead. They are not wraiths, which live on the far side of the Shroud. They are memory made spirit, the remembered strength of bloodlines. Kinfolk of all three clans are buried here, side by side, the only place they lie together.

facts.v: Gaia

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Speak of the dead with respect or not at all. Ancestor-spirits answer Garou who honour them, and they turn their backs, for a year, on anyone who mocks them.

uz-climates.name: The Three Climates
uz-climates.html: Three domes hold three kept Wylds: a jungle, a desert and a show garden. The Weaver built the glass and the Wyld filled it. Here they are the rare thing, a working partnership. The jungle-spirits are restless and want out.

facts.v: Wyld under glass

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Each climate keeps its own season. Weather-Gifts work only in the dome whose season matches them.

uz-dammed.name: The Dammed Reach
uz-dammed.sub: The Milwaukee River above the North Avenue dam
uz-dammed.html: The old North Avenue dam holds the river in a long, slow pool. The river spirit is sullen and patient behind it, collecting every word spoken over its water. It is waiting for the dam to come down, and it believes, without any evidence, that it will.

facts.v: Weaver over Wyld

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Still water keeps secrets. Anything spoken over the impounded river is remembered by it and can be called back up by anyone who knows the right question.

uz-blight.name: The Blighted Wood
uz-blight.sub: The poisoned forests of Franklin and the Root River
uz-blight.html: In late autumn 1991, while the Sabbat came into the city, the House Goratrix Tremere Jesselin and Maximus McKenzie walked the southern woods and defiled the protected places: the ward-stones, springs and sacred trees around the Bleeding Pine. Their blood magic lanced them like boils, and the Banes came through. The plan was simple: while the Garou cleaned their forest, they would have no time for the city. It worked. The pines weep black, the creeks smell of copper, and the Eagle, and sometimes the Coyote with them, have been fighting for weeks.

facts.v: Wyrm

notes.title: The law here
notes.html: Everything that guarded now bites. Wards, ward-stones and tree-signs are turned against their makers: a Gift called here answers a Bane twice as readily as a Garou, and every drop of spilled Gnosis draws more.

gz-grand.name: The Grand Warrens
gz-grand.sub: The Nosferatu’s main refuge under downtown
gz-grand.html: A network of old storm drains, the cellars of demolished buildings and abandoned pneumatic-post channels under the river’s west bank. Most of the city’s Nosferatu live here: clean, dry halls, maps on the walls, a market in rumours. Outsiders come in only with a guide.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: A guest follows the guide and asks no questions about faces.

gz-market.name: The Rat Market
gz-market.sub: An underground bazaar beneath the Third Ward
gz-market.html: The cellars of the old Commission Row warehouses, joined by knocked-through walls. The Nosferatu keep a neutral market here: information, papers, weapons, bagged blood. Since the invasion trade has halved, because everyone is afraid of the tunnels.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Trade, don’t fight. Troublemakers are handed to the Council.

gz-steam.name: The steam tunnels
gz-steam.html: Hot, cramped passages lined with district-heating pipes, joining the basements of MECCA, the Hyatt and the government buildings. The Elders use them to move between Elysia unseen. The cell where Akawa is held is down here too.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: The tunnels belong to the Council. Strangers are met by Gracis’s ghouls.

gz-null.name: The Hush under the chapel
gz-null.sub: The null zone reaches down as well
gz-null.html: Under the Marquette campus magic fails below ground as well as above. The sewers here are strangely quiet: the rats don’t squeak, the water runs without a sound. At the very bottom is the place where Usla buried the halves of two totems.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Spells fall silent. You will have to rely on your hands.

gz-brew.name: The Miller caves
gz-brew.html: Cold cellars dug into the hillside where beer once matured. A tour stop by day and a neutral meeting place by night. The Nosferatu and the Gangrel use them as a waystation.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Leave something cold for the cellars’ keeper.

gz-flesh.name: The flesh tunnels
gz-flesh.sub: Dragos’s workshops under the Menomonee Valley
gz-flesh.html: Under the old tanneries and slaughterhouses Dragos set up his workshops. In places the walls are alive: meat and bone grown into the brick. Most of the army died, but the surviving creatures came back here as to a nest, and Castor feeds them. The Nosferatu give these tunnels a wide berth.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Here, you are what’s hunted.

gz-southnest.name: The southern nests
gz-southnest.html: The wide tunnel runs north from the Cudahy warehouses. Dragos’s creatures marched to the city along it. Now loners and small packs, the ones nobody finished off, live in its side galleries.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Move fast and don’t answer the voices.

gz-sabbat.name: The Black Water cistern
gz-sabbat.sub: The last Sabbat lair · Walker’s Point
gz-sabbat.html: A flooded old cistern under Walker’s Point. The Black Water pack hides here, and Guillem Velez comes here when the yacht isn’t safe. In the cistern’s dark a Lasombra is at his strongest.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: The shadows here look back.

gz-drake.name: Drake’s den
gz-drake.html: In a forgotten part of the storm culverts under the concrete-lined river hides Drake: once Merik’s go-between, now a creature of the Wyrm. The walls are scratched with spirals.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Never walk in a spiral.

gz-vozd.name: The vozhd’s lair
gz-vozd.sub: Construction drifts of the Deep Tunnel
gz-vozd.html: An abandoned side drift of the Deep Tunnel under construction, three hundred feet underground. The vozhd sleeps here, with Parovich’s face in its flank.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Say nothing. It listens with voices.

gz-flood.name: The drowned galleries
gz-flood.sub: Old sewers under the East Side
gz-flood.html: Old brick sewers flooded when the new ones came into service. The water stands chest-deep, and something swims in it. The Nosferatu go through only on rafts.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Never put your hands in the water.

gz-pocket.name: The Michigan Pocket
gz-pocket.sub: An impossible cave under the lake
gz-pocket.html: A cave that cannot exist: a vast vault of dark stone under the bed of Lake Michigan, where for generations the local sluagh carried condemned buildings and the debris of crumbling architecture. A diner stands here, a gas station, houses, a gazebo, a boxcar, a bridge truss, a church spire and cemetery angels: everything the city decided to forget. The Pocket was once a cultural site shared by the sluagh and the Nosferatu. Since Parovich went over to the Sabbat the door has been shut. Ivory is the last faerie who looks after it.

notes.title: The rule down here
notes.html: Take nothing away. The Pocket takes, and doesn’t give back.

kd-gracis.name: Kilbourntown
kd-gracis.html: The old west-bank town Gracis ruled before the cities merged, and still treats as his. His villa, the north-side Mafia contacts and the right to feed on the Avenue bars are his by long custom.
kd-gracis.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-lucina.name: The Theatre District
kd-lucina.html: The Performing Arts Center, the Pabst Theater, the Auditorium and the Hyatt: Lucina’s by right of taste and by Gracis’s indulgence. Louis Detonas has the run of the galleries on her sufferance.
kd-lucina.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-louis.name: East Town galleries
kd-louis.html: A few blocks of galleries, studios and expensive apartments around Louis’s own. Toreador neonates come here to be noticed.
kd-louis.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-jason.name: Walker’s Point
kd-jason.html: Jason’s quiet domain around his tenement penthouse. Embarrassingly for the Council’s swing vote, the Sabbat ran its invasion from a church in his streets and its last pack still hides in a cistern beneath them.
kd-jason.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-hrothulf.name: Hrothulf’s Outlands acre
kd-hrothulf.html: His house and the cleared yards around it, deep in the Outlands. Nobody has ever contested it, and the Lupines avoid it for reasons of their own.
kd-hrothulf.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-chapel.name: The Chapel grounds
kd-chapel.html: The Highland Boulevard blocks around the chantry. Since Victor’s death Newman has extended the wards a block in every direction, and the neighbours have started sleeping badly.
kd-chapel.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-mortius.name: The haunted block
kd-mortius.html: Mortius’s own house at the null zone’s edge, which mortals swear is haunted. Its wards fail on the eastern side, where the null zone begins.
kd-mortius.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-jade.name: Jade’s tower
kd-jade.html: The Brujah Primogen’s official domain: her tower and the blocks around it, granted by the Council with a show of reluctance. She has not hunted here once.
kd-jade.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-jade2.name: Jade’s reserve haven
kd-jade2.html: Macy’s street in Wauwatosa, technically inside the Anubi patrol zone. Decker has let it stand. He hasn’t said why.
kd-jade2.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-scott.name: The Black Prince’s lakeshore (vacant)
kd-scott.html: Sir Edward Scott’s domain on the Lower East Side. Jade could claim it as Brujah Primogen; she hasn’t. Turk’s Union is quietly moving in.
kd-scott.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-parovich.name: Parovich’s Concordia (vacant)
kd-parovich.html: The decaying mansion blocks of the former Nosferatu Primogen. The Council sealed the house; Mother Agatha claims the streets for the Warrens and nobody argues, because nobody wants to go there.
kd-parovich.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-merik.name: The Prince’s block (sealed)
kd-merik.html: The penthouse block is sealed and nobody holds the Prince’s domain, which used to be the whole city. Every Council member pretends not to want it.
kd-merik.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-gunther.name: The river above the dam
kd-gunther.html: The banks and the pond above the North Avenue dam. Merik granted it to Gunther in the 1930s; nobody has had the nerve to ask whether the grant died with Merik.
kd-gunther.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-soraya.name: The folded blocks
kd-soraya.html: A few blocks on Yankee Hill that are slightly further away than they should be. The Council has never formally granted them, because the Council has never formally noticed them.
kd-soraya.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-ethan.name: Ethan’s firing lanes
kd-ethan.html: The valley rooftops Ethan can cover from his elevator. Inside Blood Brother turf, and the Brothers treat it as his.
kd-ethan.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-decker.name: The Good Hope motel strip
kd-decker.html: Decker keeps no real haven, but the motels and diners along Good Hope Road are Anubi ground by any measure.
kd-decker.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-turk.name: Turk’s riverboat & the War Memorial
kd-turk.html: The Veterans Park shore and the Art Museum steps, the heart of Union turf.
kd-turk.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-agatha.name: The Warrens
kd-agatha.html: Everything from the Grand Warrens to the harbour lock is Nosferatu ground, by a right older than the Council. Mother Agatha governs it.
kd-agatha.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-steam.name: The Council’s steam tunnels
kd-steam.html: The service tunnels between MECCA, the Hyatt and the government buildings. Gracis’s ghouls guard them for the Council, and Akawa is held somewhere inside.
kd-steam.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-castor.name: Castor’s flesh tunnels
kd-castor.html: The Tzimisce claim nothing on paper. In practice nobody else walks here.
kd-castor.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

kd-blackwater.name: The Black Water cistern
kd-blackwater.html: The last Sabbat lair in the city, right under Jason’s domain.
kd-blackwater.src: Domains are improvised on the book’s havens and the chronicle canon.

l-goodhope.name: Good Hope Road patrol
l-goodhope.html: The northern edge of Kindred territory and a favourite Anubi patrol route. Country clubs along it make perfect Lupine ambush cover. Anarchs dare each other to drive its length: “Done Good Hope” five times and you’re an Ace.

l-harbor.name: North Harbor Drive patrol
l-harbor.html: Decker recently stretched his patrols down to the lakefront here. He suspects Lupines are swimming the lake and slipping through the shore parks to meet with the Union.

l-lakeN.name: Lakefront parks: northern Lupine run
l-lakeN.html: The chain of lakeshore parks runs far north and south. Werewolves have used them as cover to reach the heart of the city, sometimes swimming the lake first.

l-lakeS.name: Lakefront parks: southern Lupine run
l-lakeS.html: South Shore, Sheridan and Grant parks give Lupines a wooded corridor from the southern Outlands nearly to Bay View.

l-i94s.name: I-94 to Chicago (Lupine-watched)
l-i94s.html: One of three highways into town, and all are said to be watched. Only the desperate drive them at night; sensible Kindred arrange a sealed daylight truck.
l-i94s.src: Milwaukee by Night, Traveling to Milwaukee, p. 8

l-i43n.name: I-43 north / Route 43 (Lupine-watched)
l-i43n.html: The northern highway out of town, where the Mask’s car was shot to pieces by the Mouse pack on Merik’s orders.
l-i43n.src: Milwaukee by Night, p. 8; A Midnight Moon

l-i894.name: I-894 bypass (Lupine-watched)
l-i894.html: Named in the book as the third major road link. Its southwestern run crosses deep into the Eagle pack’s country.

l-skywalk.name: The sky-walk
l-skywalk.html: Catwalks linking the Hyatt Regency, MECCA, the Arena, the Auditorium and the Reuss Federal Plaza. An Elder can cross the whole complex without touching the street or seeing it.

l-bridgewar.name: Bridge War line (1840s)
l-bridgewar.html: Gracis and Hrothulf fought their war through mortal pawns, claiming the quarrel was over who paid for the river bridges. In 1845 Gracis staged a riot and the bridges were destroyed. Placed at the Chestnut Street (Juneau Ave) crossing.

l-ritual.name: The ring of the four anchors
l-ritual.html: The outline of the Chapel’s ritual: four antennae on the city’s edges, aimed at the null zone. Their diagonals cross over St. Joan of Arc Chapel; the far anchors (west and north) stand about twice as far out as their partners, the proportion the Chapel’s geometry calls a “lever”. When all four are tuned, their fields close over Marquette.

l-ritual2.name: The ring of the four anchors · north–south axis
l-ritual2.html: The second diagonal of the ritual, from the Hotel Warszawa through the chapel to the Lincoln Creek mast.

l-chase.name: The dragon’s chase
l-chase.html: The path of Dragos Dalca in dragon form: from the Cudahy warehouses over Bay View, where the cameras caught him, to the fish plant where Jade killed him.

tr-white.name: The White Flag Crossing

facts.v: Cross with a small white cloth openly displayed and name someone on the far bank you mean to meet peacefully.
About twenty minutes, usually.

The Tollman can dispute who counts as a resident of either bank. The road reads intention, not justice: an armed traveller with a peaceful purpose may pass, and someone hiding a planned attack is refused.
A failed crossing returns you to your starting bank.

tr-white.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-borrow.name: The Borrower’s Stair

facts.v: In the dreaming basement stacks, return an unfinished work of your own to the shelf where it belongs and state the question that stopped you. A ladder descends from above, although you are underground.
Ten minutes to the reception desk; unpredictable beyond.
Follow a shelf because it holds the answer you want rather than the work you borrowed, and companions split into separate lines of inquiry. Agree on a meeting question first.
Mrs. Quire keeps a return slip for every admitted visitor and wants a better explanation each time she has to fetch one.

tr-borrow.sub: Ten minutes to the reception desk; unpredictable beyond.
tr-borrow.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-unbuilt.name: The Unbuilt Stair

facts.v: Climb a staircase while describing a specific thing you intend to build, teach or repair.
About half an hour.
Declare grander plans than you really intend and doors to much larger responsibilities open for you.
Return down the same stair carrying a tangible record of a small step already completed. This is why Kit carries so many receipts.

tr-unbuilt.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 22. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-lantern.name: The Lantern Wake

facts.v: Carry a properly kindled scale-light lantern in an enchanted vessel, with a chart from Ruth or the Ashen Usher.
One long night, even when the mountain looks close.
Follow the lantern’s reflection, not the star you most want to reach. A wind that blows the wake ahead of the bow is the clear warning to turn back.
Keep one full charge for the way home. Bjorn has the only known working lantern.

tr-lantern.sub: One long night, even when the mountain looks close.
tr-lantern.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, pp. 16, 22–23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-line.name: The Third Shift Line

facts.v: Leon’s consent, and a ticket punched with the date you expect to return.
Planned at fifteen minutes. Currently unsafe for passengers.
The Glass shard recognises old wartime destinations as unserved stops. The fix is to replace it with an honest mechanism, not to learn to exploit it.
If restored, one short reliable municipal route; the repaired Bell can call a ticketed passenger back.

tr-line.sub: Planned at fifteen minutes. Currently unsafe for passengers.
tr-line.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, pp. 8, 23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-candle.name: The Low Candle Way

facts.v: Ivory’s invitation, and the correct physical approach through the warrens.
Short, when she opens it.
Being seen at its mortal entrance can expose your movements to Nosferatu observation, though that gives no access to the freehold. The outer court has no sign of anything beyond it.
Only as Ivory permits.

tr-candle.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-platform.name: To the Waiting Platform

facts.v: An actual invitation from a named destination outside Milwaukee.
The platform is reachable; onward service is not dependable.
The timetable shows persuasive departures that cannot carry a living traveller home.
Walk back up into the Ward. Ordinary buses and trains still leave town in daylight.

tr-platform.sub: The platform is reachable; onward service is not dependable.
tr-platform.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 23. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-chicago.name: The old Chicago road

facts.v: None that works.
Every departing train carries the name of someone who abandoned Milwaukee.
It ends at the Waiting Platform. Reopening one trustworthy outward trod is Ruth’s project.

tr-chicago.sub: Every departing train carries the name of someone who abandoned Milwaukee.
tr-chicago.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 9. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

tr-depart.name: The Far Guest’s road

facts.v: None.
The route the dragon used to leave Earth.
Severed. It cannot currently be followed, and it isn’t this chronicle’s inevitable destination.

tr-depart.sub: The route the dragon used to leave Earth.
tr-depart.src: Milwaukee: The Unclaimed City, p. 17. Entry customs negotiate with a particular road; performing one does not give anyone access to the Dreaming.

facts.v: The Hierarchy’s procession route from the Citadel to the registry at Forest Home, following the line of old funeral corteges. Legionnaires keep it lit with corpse-candles.
Renegades ambush prisoner details where the road crosses the valley.
The Grim Legion’s marching road along Wisconsin Avenue and Bluemound. The Ninth Watch patrols the eastern half.
Dawn wind through the Marquette anomaly can blow travellers off the road and into strange Shroud weather.
The relic Milwaukee Road line south to the Chicago Necropolis. Sealed cars, Harbinger escorts, departures on the hour of a death.
Stowaways are Reaped on arrival in Chicago.
The drowned excursion steamer runs as a ferry across the Sea of Shadows toward Chicago. Centurion Dolan won’t take a passenger who can’t name someone waiting for them on the far shore.
Maelstrom weather. Spectres follow her wake, and some nights her own dead forget they are crew.
The Renegades’ route from Bay View into downtown along Kinnickinnic and the river, the way the strikers marched.
Hierarchy patrols watch the bridges, and the Newhall end is Spectre country.
A path of relic stairs and alleys from Walnut Street down to the lake that only the free wraiths keep. Lorraine’s people use it to reach the newly dead before the Reapers.
Where it crosses the Freeway the Hollow pulls at anyone who looks down.
A Tempest byway from the Interchange Hollow under the river and out beneath the lake. Smugglers use it to move what the Usurers won’t list.
Spectres. The Labyrinth lies somewhere below.
In hard winters the Sea of Shadows freezes along a line toward the Far Shores. Walkers who reach the end do not come back to say what is there.
It only exists while the living lake is frozen. Thaw while you are on it and you go into the Tempest.

up-cm.name: Moon bridge: Grinning Stone to the Granary
up-cm.html: The last open moon bridge in the city, until this autumn. Horatio and Rosa kept it open as a courtesy, and they were the only two leaders who still talked. On the night the Granary was defiled the span snapped in the middle, and now it hangs in the sky in two flickering stumps. Mercer can’t raise it alone, and Horatio’s Red Talons aren’t sure they want a bridge into the human city at all.

up-em.name: Moon bridge: Bleeding Pine to the Granary
up-em.html: Broken in the 1930s, when Merik used Erica’s friendship with the Mouse to set them against the Eagle. The span still hangs half-built in the sky, flickering.

up-ce.name: The bridge that was never built
up-ce.html: Coyote and Eagle have never opened a moon bridge between their caerns. The Lunes keep a ghost-span in the sky anyway, out of hope or mockery. Since both clans started fighting Banes in the same forest, the ghost glows a little brighter.

up-hh.name: The cold bridge to the Hill
up-hh.html: A dead moon bridge to the sealed caern on Holy Hill. It would light up if the caern were reopened.

up-chi.name: The Chicago bridge
up-chi.html: Once the Mouse ran a moon bridge south to the Chicago caerns. The Weaver’s airport spindle cut it in the 1950s, and the Pattern Spiders have kept it cut. The Glass Walkers of Chicago still don’t know the Mouse are gone.

up-usla.name: Usla’s Last Crawl
up-usla.html: The track of the dying Usla from the buried relics to the lake, still glowing faintly in the Penumbra three centuries later. Follow it and you feel his shame and his exhaustion. At the end Greatwater is waiting.

up-fog.name: The Fog Road
up-fog.html: When the Grey Coming rolls in, fog-spirits walk up the river from the harbor to the North Avenue dam, carrying Greatwater’s whispers into the heart of the city.

up-smelt.name: The Smelt Run
up-smelt.html: Every spring the smelt run along the shore by night, and the whole lakefront crowds with lanterns and nets. Their spirit is a silver road that small spirits ride north and south. In autumn it is only a faint shimmer.

up-decay.name: Riding the Winds of Decay
